gen-1-28: God blessed the first people and gave them the work of filling the earth and ruling over it as His representatives, so human life and work have purpose under Him.
gen-1-29: God gave the first people the seed-bearing plants and fruit trees of the earth as food, providing generously for those He made.
gen-3-15: God promises that the woman's offspring will crush the serpent's head while being wounded himself, long read as the first announcement of Christ's victory over evil.
gen-8-21: God promises never again to curse the ground or destroy every living thing as in the flood, out of mercy even though the human heart is bent toward evil.
gen-8-22: God promises that as long as the earth remains, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, and day and night will not cease.
gen-9-1: After the flood, God blessed Noah and his sons and renewed the call to be fruitful and fill the earth, so life begins again under His favor.
gen-9-9-11: God promises in His covenant with Noah, his descendants and every living creature that a flood will never again destroy all life on the earth.
gen-9-12-16: God promises that the rainbow is the sign of His everlasting covenant with all living creatures, and when He sees it He will remember never to flood the earth again.
gen-12-2-3: God promises Abram a great nation, a great name and His blessing, and that all the families of the earth will be blessed through him, fulfilled in Christ.
gen-12-7: God promises to give the land of Canaan to Abram's offspring, and Abram responds by building an altar to the LORD.
gen-13-14-17: God promises Abram all the land he can see in every direction, for him and his offspring forever, with descendants as countless as the dust of the earth.
gen-15-1: God tells Abram not to be afraid, because God Himself is his shield and his exceedingly great reward.
gen-15-4-5: God promises the childless Abram a son from his own body and descendants as countless as the stars.
gen-15-13-14: God tells Abram his offspring will be oppressed as foreigners for four hundred years, but promises to judge that nation and bring them out with great wealth.
gen-15-18: God makes a covenant with Abram, promising his offspring the land from the river of Egypt to the Euphrates.
gen-16-10: God promises the mistreated servant Hagar, through His angel, that her offspring will be too many to count.
gen-17-4-8: God promises Abraham an everlasting covenant: he will be the father of many nations and kings, God will be God to his offspring, and Canaan will be theirs forever.
gen-17-15-16: God promises to bless Sarah and give Abraham a son by her, so that she becomes the mother of nations and kings.
gen-17-19: God promises that Sarah will bear Abraham a son named Isaac and that His everlasting covenant will continue through Isaac's offspring.
gen-17-20: God promises Abraham that He has heard his prayer for Ishmael: Ishmael will be blessed, father twelve princes and become a great nation.
gen-18-10: God promises Abraham that by the same time next year his elderly wife Sarah will have a son.
gen-18-14: Nothing is too hard for the LORD; God promises again that at the appointed time Sarah will have a son.
gen-21-12: God tells Abraham to listen to Sarah, promising that his offspring will be named through Isaac, even in a painful family decision.
gen-21-17-18: God heard the boy Ishmael crying in the desert and promises Hagar, through His angel, that He will make him a great nation.
gen-22-17-18: God swears to bless Abraham, multiply his offspring like the stars and sand, and bless all nations through his offspring, because Abraham obeyed His voice.
gen-26-3-4: God promises Isaac, during famine, to be with him, bless him, give the land to his offspring and keep the oath He swore to Abraham.
gen-26-24: God tells Isaac not to be afraid and promises His presence, His blessing and many descendants for His servant Abraham's sake.
gen-28-13-15: God promises the fleeing Jacob the land, countless offspring, blessing for all families through him, and His protection wherever he goes until every promise is kept.
gen-31-3: God tells Jacob to return to the land of his fathers and promises to be with him.
gen-35-10-12: God renames Jacob Israel and promises him a nation and many nations, kings among his descendants, and the land given to Abraham and Isaac.
gen-46-3-4: God tells Jacob not to fear going to Egypt, promising to go with him, make his family a great nation there and surely bring them back.
gen-48-21: God would be with Joseph and bring the family back to the land of their fathers, as the dying Jacob confidently declares.
gen-50-24: God would surely come to help Israel and bring them out of Egypt to the land He swore to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, as the dying Joseph declares.
exo-3-7-8: God has seen His people's affliction in Egypt and heard their cry, and He promises to rescue them and bring them into a good land flowing with milk and honey.
exo-3-12: God promises Moses, "Certainly I will be with you," with the sign that Israel will worship Him on this mountain after leaving Egypt.
exo-3-14: God reveals His name as "I AM WHO I AM": He exists in Himself, never changes and depends on no one.
exo-4-12: God promises the hesitant Moses that He will be with his mouth and teach him what to say.
exo-6-2-8: God remembers His covenant and promises Israel: "I will bring you out, redeem you, take you as My people, be your God and bring you into the land."
exo-12-13: God promises the Israelites in Egypt that when He sees the lamb's blood on their houses, He will pass over them and the plague will not destroy them.
exo-14-13-14: God would fight for Israel at the sea, so they were told not to fear but stand still and see His salvation that day.
exo-15-2: God is the strength, song and salvation of His rescued people, the God of their fathers whom they praise and exalt.
exo-15-13: God, in His loving kindness, leads the people He has redeemed and guides them by His strength to His holy dwelling.
exo-15-26: God promises Israel that if they listen to Him and keep His commandments, He will not bring Egypt's diseases on them, for He is the LORD who heals.
exo-16-4: God promises to rain bread from heaven for Israel each day, testing whether they will gather only a day's portion and walk in His law.
exo-16-12: God heard Israel's complaints and promises meat in the evening and bread in the morning, so they will know He is the LORD their God.
exo-19-4-6: God, who carried Israel on eagles' wings, promises that if they obey Him and keep His covenant, they will be His treasured possession, a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.
exo-20-2: God introduces His commandments by declaring who He is: the LORD their God, who brought them out of slavery in Egypt. His rescue comes before His commands.
exo-20-5-6: God forbids idol worship and warns of judgment on those who hate Him, but promises loving kindness to thousands who love Him and keep His commandments.
exo-20-12: God commands Israel to honor father and mother and promises long life in the land He gives them, the first commandment with a promise.
exo-23-20-22: God promises Israel an angel to guard them and bring them to the prepared place; if they obey him, God will oppose their enemies.
exo-23-25-26: God promises Israel that if they serve Him, He will bless their bread and water, remove sickness, prevent miscarriage and barrenness, and fulfill their days in the land.
exo-23-29-30: God promises to drive out Canaan's nations little by little, not in one year, so the land stays inhabitable until Israel grows enough to inherit it.
exo-29-45-46: God promises to dwell among Israel and be their God, so they will know He brought them out of Egypt in order to live among them.
exo-33-14: God promises Moses, "My presence will go with you, and I will give you rest."
exo-33-17: God promises to do what Moses asked and keep going with Israel, because Moses has found favor with Him and He knows him by name.
exo-33-19: God promises to make all His goodness pass before Moses and proclaim His name; His grace and mercy are His to give freely.
exo-34-6-7: God proclaims His character: merciful, gracious, slow to anger, abounding in loving kindness and truth, forgiving sin, yet never clearing the guilty.
exo-34-10: God promises, in renewing His covenant, to do marvels never done in any nation, so all the peoples around Israel will see His awesome work.
lev-26-3-6: God promises Israel that if they keep His commandments, He will send rain in season, abundant harvests, and peace and safety in their land.
lev-26-9-12: God promises obedient Israel fruitfulness, plenty and above all His presence: He will dwell among them, walk among them and be their God.
lev-26-13: God is the LORD who brought Israel out of Egypt, broke the bars of their yoke and made them walk upright as free people.
lev-26-40-42: God promises that if scattered Israel confesses its sin and humbles its heart, He will remember His covenant with Jacob, Isaac and Abraham, and the land.
lev-26-44-45: God promises that even in enemy lands He will not utterly reject Israel or break His covenant, but will remember the covenant with their ancestors.
num-6-24-26: God gave His priests this blessing for Israel: that the LORD would bless and keep them, shine His face on them with grace, and give them peace.
num-10-33-34: God guided Israel from Sinai, with the ark going ahead to find them a resting place and His cloud over them by day.
num-14-17-19: God is slow to anger and abundant in loving kindness, and on that basis Moses prays for Him to pardon His rebellious people.
num-14-20-21: God pardoned Israel in answer to Moses' prayer and swore that all the earth will be filled with His glory, though that generation still faced consequences.
num-15-40-41: God gave tassels as reminders to obey His commandments and be holy, because He is the LORD who brought Israel out of Egypt to be their God.
num-21-8-9: God promises that anyone bitten by the snakes who looks at the bronze serpent will live, a picture Jesus later applied to His cross.
num-23-19-20: God is not a man who lies or changes His mind; what He has spoken He will do, and the blessing He gives cannot be reversed.
num-23-21: God is with Israel as their King, and the oracle declares that He has not seen iniquity in Jacob to curse.
num-24-5-7: God has planted Israel like well-watered gardens and cedars, and the oracle foresees their growth and an exalted king.
num-24-17: God reveals through Balaam that a star and scepter will rise from Israel to defeat its enemies, fulfilled in David and linked by Christians to the Messiah.
deu-1-29-31: God goes before His people and fights for them, as He did in Egypt, and carried them through the wilderness as a father carries his son.
deu-2-7: God blessed the work of Israel's hands, watched over their journey and was with them for forty years in the wilderness, so they lacked nothing.
deu-4-7: God is near to His people whenever they call on Him, unlike the gods of any other nation.
deu-4-29-31: God promises that scattered Israel will find Him when they seek Him with all their heart, because He is merciful and will not forget His covenant.
deu-4-39-40: God alone is God in heaven and on earth, and He promises that keeping His commandments will bring good to Israel and their children and long life in the land.
deu-5-9-10: God forbids idol worship and warns those who hate Him, but promises loving kindness to thousands who love Him and keep His commandments.
deu-5-29: God longs for His people to have hearts that fear Him and keep His commandments always, so that it may go well with them and their children forever.
deu-6-4-5: God is the LORD, the one God, and He calls His people to love Him with all their heart, soul and strength, the commandment Jesus called the greatest.
deu-7-6-8: God chose Israel as His treasured people, not because they were many, but because He loved them and kept the oath He swore to their fathers.
deu-7-9: God is the faithful God who keeps His covenant and loving kindness for a thousand generations with those who love Him and keep His commandments.
deu-7-12-13: God promises Israel that if they keep His ordinances, He will keep His covenant love, bless their families, crops and herds, and multiply them in the land.
deu-7-15: God promises covenant Israel that He will take away sickness and keep the diseases of Egypt from them in the land, a promise to the nation under His covenant.
deu-8-2-4: God led Israel forty years in the wilderness to humble and test them, feeding them manna to teach that people live by every word from His mouth.
deu-8-7-10: God promises to bring Israel into a good land of water, grain, fruit and minerals where they will lack nothing, and they are to bless Him when satisfied.
deu-8-15-16: God led Israel through a dangerous wilderness, gave water from rock and manna, humbling and testing them to do them good in the end.
deu-9-3: God promises to go before Israel as a consuming fire and subdue the nations of Canaan, so the victory is His, not theirs.
deu-10-12-13: God asks His people to fear Him, walk in His ways, love and serve Him wholeheartedly and keep His commandments, which He gives for their good.
deu-10-17-19: God is God of gods and Lord of lords, takes no bribes, defends the fatherless and widow and loves the foreigner, so His people must love foreigners too.
deu-11-11-12: God cares for the land He gives Israel, and His eyes are on it from the beginning of the year to the end.
deu-11-18-21: God calls Israel to keep His words in their hearts and teach them to their children, promising that their days will be multiplied in the land He swore to give.
deu-11-26-28: God sets before Israel a blessing if they obey His commandments and a curse if they turn away to other gods.
deu-12-9-10: God promises that once Israel crosses the Jordan, He will give them rest from all their enemies so they live in safety.
deu-15-4-6: God promises Israel that if they fully obey Him, He will bless them in the land so no one need remain poor, and they will lend to nations rather than borrow.
deu-18-15-18: God promises to raise up a prophet like Moses from among Israel and put His words in his mouth, fulfilled ultimately in Jesus.
deu-20-1-4: God promises Israel in battle that He goes with them to fight their enemies and save them, so they must not fear stronger armies.
deu-23-5: God refused to listen to Balaam and turned his curse into a blessing for Israel, because He loved them.
deu-23-14: God walks in the middle of Israel's camp to deliver them and defeat their enemies, so their camp must be kept holy.
deu-26-17-19: God declares Israel His treasured possession, as He promised, and will set them high in praise, name and honor as a people holy to Him.
deu-28-1-6: God promises Israel that if they diligently obey Him, He will set them above the nations and bless them in city and field, family, herds, food, coming and going.
deu-28-7-8: God promises obedient Israel that He will defeat their attackers and command blessing on their barns and work in the land, a national covenant blessing.
deu-28-11-12: God promises obedient Israel abundant children, livestock and crops, rain in its season from His storehouse, and blessing on their work, so they lend and do not borrow.
deu-30-1-3: God promises that when scattered Israel returns to Him and obeys with all their heart, He will have compassion, restore them and gather them from the nations.
deu-30-4-6: God promises to gather Israel from the farthest places, bring them into the land and circumcise their hearts to love Him with all their heart and live.
deu-30-8-10: God promises that when Israel turns back and obeys Him wholeheartedly, He will again delight to prosper their work, families, livestock and land.
deu-30-11-14: God's command is not too hard or far away; His word is near, in His people's mouth and heart, so they can do it, as Paul echoes in Romans 10.
deu-30-15-16: God sets before Israel life and death, and promises that loving Him and keeping His ways will bring life, growth and blessing in the land.
deu-30-19-20: God calls Israel to choose life by loving Him, obeying Him and holding fast to Him, for He is their life and length of days in the land.
deu-31-6: God promises Israel entering Canaan that He Himself goes with them and will not fail or forsake them, so they can be strong and courageous.
deu-31-8: God promises Joshua that He goes before him, will be with him and will not fail or forsake him, so he need not fear or be discouraged.
deu-32-9-10: God's people are His own portion; He found them in a barren wilderness, surrounded them, cared for them and kept them as the apple of His eye.
deu-32-11-12: God cared for Israel like an eagle spreading its wings to carry its young; the LORD alone led them, with no foreign god beside Him.
deu-32-36: God promises to judge His people yet have compassion on His servants when He sees their strength is gone.
deu-32-39: God alone is God: He puts to death and makes alive, wounds and heals, and no one can deliver out of His hand.
deu-33-12: God's beloved tribe of Benjamin will dwell securely beside Him, sheltered by Him all day long.
deu-33-26-27: God rides the heavens to help His people; the eternal God is their dwelling place, and underneath are the everlasting arms.
deu-33-29: God saved Israel and is their shield and sword, so they are a happy people whose enemies will submit to them.
jos-1-3-5: God promises Joshua every place his foot treads in the land, that no one will stand against him, and that as He was with Moses He will never fail or forsake him.
jos-1-6-7: God commands Joshua to be strong and very courageous as he leads Israel into the land, carefully obeying all the law of Moses so that he may succeed wherever he goes.
jos-1-8-9: God tells Joshua to meditate on His law day and night and obey it so his way will prosper, and promises to be with him wherever he goes.
jos-3-7: God promises to begin exalting Joshua before Israel that day, so they will know He is with Joshua as He was with Moses.
jos-6-2: God tells Joshua that He has already given Jericho, its king and its warriors into his hand, before a single wall fell.
jos-10-8: God tells Joshua not to fear the attacking kings, for He has delivered them into his hands and none of them will stand before him.
jos-14-9: God's promise through Moses gave Caleb the land he had walked on as an inheritance for him and his children, because he wholly followed the LORD.
jos-21-43-45: God gave Israel all the land He swore to their fathers and gave them rest; not one of His good promises to Israel failed, and all came to pass.
jos-23-10-11: God fought for Israel as He promised, so one of them could chase a thousand; therefore they must take care to love the LORD their God.
jos-23-14: God kept every good thing He spoke concerning Israel; not one of His promises failed, as the dying Joshua reminds them.
1sa-2-1-2: God is holy like no other, the Rock beside whom there is no one, and Hannah rejoices in His salvation after He answered her prayer for a son.
1sa-2-6-8: God rules over life and death, poverty and wealth; He lifts the poor from the dust and the needy from the ash heap to sit with princes.
1sa-2-9-10: God guards the steps of His faithful ones while the wicked are silenced, for no one prevails by strength; He will judge the earth and strengthen His anointed king.
1sa-7-12: God helped Israel to that very point, and Samuel set up the Ebenezer stone as a reminder: "The LORD helped us until now."
1sa-12-22: God will not forsake His people for His great name's sake, because it pleased Him to make them His own, even after they sinned by demanding a king.
1sa-16-7: God does not see as people see; people look at outward appearance, but the LORD looks at the heart.
2sa-7-8-11: God, who took David from the sheep pen to be king, promises him a great name, a secure home for Israel, rest from his enemies and a lasting house.
2sa-7-12-13: God promises David that his offspring will succeed him, build a house for God's name and have his throne established forever, fulfilled finally in Jesus, the Son of David.
2sa-7-14-16: God promises to be a father to David's heir, disciplining him when he sins but never removing His loving kindness, and to establish David's house and throne forever.
2sa-22-2-4: God is David's rock, fortress, deliverer, shield and refuge; David called on the LORD and was saved from his enemies.
2sa-22-29-31: God is a lamp who lights up darkness and gives strength for battle; His way is perfect, His word is proven, and He shields all who take refuge in Him.
2sa-22-33-34: God is David's strong fortress, who made his way secure and gave him feet like a deer's to stand on the heights.
1ki-3-12-14: God gives Solomon the wise heart he asked for, adds riches and honor he did not ask for, and promises long life if he walks in God's ways as David did.
1ki-6-12-13: God promises Solomon that if he walks in His statutes, He will fulfill His word to David, dwell among Israel and not forsake His people.
1ki-8-56: God has given His people rest as He promised; not one word of all His good promise through Moses has failed.
1ki-9-3: God tells Solomon He has heard his prayer and consecrated the temple to put His name there, with His eyes and heart there, conditional on Israel's faithfulness.
2ki-6-16: God's unseen forces outnumbered the enemy around Elisha, who told his frightened servant not to fear before God opened the servant's eyes to see them.
2ki-19-30-31: God promises besieged Judah that a surviving remnant will take root again and bear fruit, and His own zeal will accomplish it.
2ki-20-5: God tells the dying King Hezekiah that He has heard his prayer and seen his tears, and promises to heal him so he will go up to the temple in three days.
1ch-16-34: God is good and His loving kindness endures forever, so His people are called to give thanks to Him.
1ch-17-11-14: God promises David a son who will build His house, to be his father and never remove His loving kindness, and to establish his throne forever in God's kingdom.
1ch-28-20: God would be with Solomon and not fail or forsake him until the temple work was finished, so David urges him to be strong, courageous and unafraid.
1ch-29-11-12: God owns the greatness, power, glory and majesty of heaven and earth; riches, honor and strength come from His hand, and He rules over all.
2ch-7-14: God promises that if His people humble themselves, pray, seek His face and turn from their wicked ways, He will hear from heaven, forgive their sin and heal their land.
2ch-7-15-16: God promises Solomon that His eyes will be open and His ears attentive to prayer made at the temple He has chosen, where His name, eyes and heart will be.
2ch-15-2: God is with His people while they are with Him; if they seek Him, He will be found, but if they forsake Him, He will forsake them.
2ch-15-7: God promises King Asa and Judah, through the prophet Azariah, that their work of reform will be rewarded, so they should be strong and not lose heart.
2ch-16-9: God's eyes range throughout the whole earth to show Himself strong for those whose hearts are fully devoted to Him; Asa acted foolishly by relying on a foreign king.
2ch-20-15-17: God tells Judah facing a vast army not to fear, for the battle is His; they need only take their positions and see His salvation, because He is with them.
2ch-20-20: God's people are called to believe in Him and His prophets, so that they will be established and succeed, as King Jehoshaphat urged Judah before battle.
ezr-8-22: God's gracious hand is on all who seek Him, but His power and wrath are against all who forsake Him, which is why Ezra would not ask the king for soldiers.
ezr-8-31: God's hand was on the returning exiles and protected them from enemies and bandits all the way to Jerusalem.
neh-1-8-9: God warned through Moses that unfaithfulness would bring exile but promised to gather those who return to Him, and Nehemiah prays for Him to remember that word.
neh-2-20: God would give success to His servants rebuilding Jerusalem's walls, Nehemiah declares to their mockers, who had no share in the city.
neh-8-10: God's holy day called for celebration and generous sharing rather than grief, for the joy of the LORD is His people's strength.
neh-9-17: God is ready to pardon, gracious, merciful, slow to anger and abundant in loving kindness, and He did not forsake His people despite their rebellion.
neh-9-19-21: God's great mercy did not forsake Israel in the wilderness: His cloud and fire guided them, His Spirit taught them, and for forty years they lacked nothing.
job-1-21: God gives and God takes away, and even after losing his children and wealth, Job blesses the LORD's name.
job-5-17-18: God's correction can lead to blessing, since He wounds and heals, as Job's friend Eliphaz says; yet God later rebukes the friends' view of Job's suffering.
job-8-20-21: God does not reject the blameless, Bildad tells Job, wrongly implying his suffering must be punishment; God later corrects Job's friends.
job-11-13-15: Zophar urges Job to turn his heart to God and put away sin to live without shame or fear, wrongly assuming Job's suffering came from hidden sin.
job-12-9-10: God's hand is behind all creation; the life of every living thing and the breath of all people are in His hand.
job-13-15: Even if God should slay him and hope seems gone, Job will still bring his case before God rather than turn away.
job-14-14-15: Job wonders whether the dead will live again and longs for the day God would call and he would answer, with God longing for the work of His hands.
job-16-19: In anguish, Job insists that even now his witness is in heaven and the one who vouches for him is on high.
job-19-25-27: Job declares that his Redeemer lives and will stand upon the earth at the last, and that even after his body is destroyed he will see God with his own eyes.
job-22-21-23: Eliphaz urges Job to be at peace with God, receive His instruction and return to Him; the call is sound, but his accusations against Job were mistaken.
job-23-10: God knows the way Job takes, and Job trusts that after being tested he will come out like gold.
job-23-13-14: God is unique and no one can oppose Him; He does what He desires and will carry out what He has appointed.
job-33-27-28: God redeems the one who confesses sin from going down to the pit so his life sees the light, as Elihu describes the aim of God's discipline.
job-36-7: God never takes His eyes off the righteous and can exalt them like kings on a throne, Elihu argues, though his verdict on Job is mixed.
job-36-15-16: God delivers the afflicted through their affliction and opens their ears in oppression, Elihu says, wanting to lead Job out of distress into freedom.
job-42-2: God can do all things, and no purpose of His can be stopped, as Job humbly confesses.
job-42-10: God restored Job's fortunes when he prayed for his friends and gave him twice as much as before.
job-42-12: God blessed the latter part of Job's life more than the beginning, a gracious restoration rather than a reward Job had demanded.
psa-1-1-3: God promises that the one who shuns the counsel of the wicked and delights in His law will be like a fruitful, well-watered tree whose leaf does not wither.
psa-2-7-8: God declares His anointed king to be His son and offers him the nations as his inheritance, words the New Testament applies to Jesus.
psa-3-3-4: God is a shield around David, his glory and the one who lifts his head; when David cries to Him, He answers from His holy hill.
psa-3-5-6: God sustained David so he could lie down, sleep and wake again, and he will not fear the tens of thousands set against him.
psa-4-3: God has set apart the godly for Himself, and David is confident the LORD hears when he calls.
psa-4-8: God alone makes David dwell in safety, so he can lie down and sleep in peace.
psa-5-11-12: God defends those who take refuge in Him, and He promises to bless the righteous and surround them with favor like a shield.
psa-8-3-5: God, who made the moon and stars, still remembers and cares for human beings and has crowned them with glory and honor.
psa-9-9-10: God is a high tower for the oppressed in times of trouble, and He has never forsaken those who seek Him.
psa-9-18: God promises that the needy will not always be forgotten, and the hope of the poor will not perish forever.
psa-10-17-18: God hears the desire of the humble, strengthens their hearts and defends the fatherless and oppressed, so that mere mortals will terrify no more.
psa-11-1: God is David's refuge, so he refuses the advice to flee like a bird to the mountains.
psa-12-5: God promises to arise because of the oppression of the weak and the groaning of the needy, and to set them in safety from those who malign them.
psa-14-5-6: God is present with the righteous, and the LORD is the refuge of the poor even when evildoers mock their plans.
psa-16-8-11: God at David's right hand keeps him from being shaken, will not abandon him to the grave and shows him the path of life and fullness of joy.
psa-17-8: David asks God to keep him as the apple of His eye and hide him in the shadow of His wings.
psa-18-1-3: God is David's strength, rock, fortress, deliverer, shield and high tower; when David called on the LORD, he was saved from his enemies.
psa-18-30: God's way is perfect and His word is proven true; He is a shield to all who take refuge in Him.
psa-19-7-11: God's law is perfect, restoring the soul, giving wisdom and joy, and more precious than gold; in keeping it there is great reward.
psa-20-6-7: God saves His anointed king and answers him with saving strength; His people trust in the LORD's name rather than in chariots and horses.
psa-22-24: God did not despise the affliction of the sufferer or hide His face from him, but heard when he cried out.
psa-22-26-27: God promises that the humble who seek Him will eat and be satisfied, and that all the ends of the earth will remember Him, turn to Him and worship.
psa-23-1-4: God is David's shepherd, providing, restoring and guiding him, and staying with him even in the valley of the shadow of death, so he fears no evil.
psa-23-5-6: God prepares a table for David before his enemies and fills his cup, and David is sure His goodness and loving kindness will follow him all his days.
psa-24-3-5: God promises that those who live uprightly, with clean hands and a pure heart, will enter His holy presence and receive His blessing.
psa-25-8-10: God is good and upright, so He teaches sinners the way and guides the humble; all His paths are loving kindness and truth to those who keep His covenant.
psa-25-14: God shares His friendship with those who fear Him and promises to make His covenant known to them.
psa-27-1: God is David's light, salvation and the strength of his life, so he has no one to fear.
psa-27-4-5: God's presence is David's one desire, and he trusts that in the day of trouble God will hide him in His shelter and set him on a rock.
psa-27-10: God will take David in even if his father and mother forsake him.
psa-27-13-14: God's goodness is something David is confident he will see in the land of the living, so he urges: be strong, take courage and wait for the LORD.
psa-28-6-7: God heard David's cry for mercy; the LORD is his strength and shield, and because he trusted Him he was helped and now sings thanks.
psa-28-8-9: God is the strength of His people and a stronghold for His anointed, and David asks Him to save, bless and shepherd His people forever.
psa-29-11: God, whose voice rules over the storm, will give strength to His people and bless them with peace.
psa-30-5: God's anger lasts only a moment, but His favor lasts a lifetime; weeping may stay for the night, but joy comes in the morning.
psa-31-5: God, the faithful Redeemer, receives David's life into His hands, the words Jesus prayed on the cross.
psa-31-19-20: God has stored up great goodness for those who fear Him and hides those who take refuge in Him from human plots and accusing tongues.
psa-31-23-24: God preserves the faithful and repays the proud, so all who hope in the LORD are called to love Him, be strong and take courage.
psa-32-1-2: God's forgiveness brings true happiness to the one whose sin is covered and whose guilt the LORD no longer counts against him.
psa-32-7-8: God is a hiding place who surrounds David with songs of deliverance, and He promises to teach and guide him in the way he should go, watching over him.
psa-33-4-5: God's word is right and all His work is faithful. He loves righteousness and justice, and the whole earth is full of His loving kindness.
psa-33-18-22: God promises to watch over those who fear Him and hope in His loving kindness, delivering them from death and keeping them alive in famine as their help and shield.
psa-34-4-7: God answered David and delivered him from all his fears; those who look to Him are radiant, and His angel encamps around those who fear Him.
psa-34-8: God's goodness is something to taste and see, and blessed is the one who takes refuge in Him.
psa-34-15-18: God's eyes are on the righteous and His ears hear their cry; He delivers them and is near to the brokenhearted, saving those crushed in spirit.
psa-34-19-22: God promises that though the righteous face many afflictions, He delivers them out of them all, and none who take refuge in Him will be condemned.
psa-35-9-10: God has no equal; He rescues the poor and needy from those too strong for them, and David vows to rejoice in His salvation.
psa-36-5-9: God's loving kindness reaches the heavens; people take refuge under His wings, feast on His abundance and drink from His spring of life.
psa-37-3-6: God promises that those who trust Him, do good and delight in Him will receive their heart's desires, and He will make their righteousness shine like the noonday sun.
psa-37-7-8: God calls His people to rest in Him and wait patiently instead of fretting over the success of the wicked, because anger leads only to evil.
psa-37-23-24: God establishes the steps of the one whose way pleases Him; though he stumbles, he will not fall, for the LORD holds him by the hand.
psa-37-25-26: God's care for the righteous is what David saw over a long life: he never saw them forsaken or their children begging, and they give generously.
psa-37-39-40: God is the salvation of the righteous and their stronghold in trouble; He helps and rescues them because they take refuge in Him.
psa-39-7: God is David's only hope when he is overwhelmed by the shortness of life.
psa-40-1-3: God heard David's patient cry, lifted him from the pit, set his feet on a rock and gave him a new song that leads many to trust Him.
psa-40-11: David asks God not to withhold His tender mercies and to let His loving kindness and truth keep him continually.
psa-41-1-3: God promises to deliver, protect and sustain on the sickbed the one who considers the poor.
psa-42-5: God remains the psalmist's hope when his soul is downcast, and he tells himself he will yet praise Him for the help of His presence.
psa-42-8: God commands His loving kindness by day, and at night His song is with the psalmist, a prayer to the God of his life.
psa-43-3-5: In a prayer from despair, God's light and truth are sought to lead back to His presence, and the troubled soul is urged to hope in God, its Savior.
psa-44-6-8: God, not bow or sword, saved Israel from their enemies, so they boast in Him all day and give thanks to His name.
psa-46-1-3: God promises to be His people's refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble, so they need not fear even if the earth gives way and the seas roar.
psa-46-10-11: God commands, "Be still, and know that I am God," for He will be exalted among the nations; the LORD of Armies is with His people as their refuge.
psa-47-8-9: God reigns over the nations from His holy throne. The rulers of the peoples gather as the people of Abraham's God, because every power on earth belongs to Him.
psa-48-14: God is His people's God forever and ever, and He will guide them even to death.
psa-49-15: God will redeem the psalmist from the power of the grave and receive him, something no wealth can buy.
psa-50-15: God promises that when His people call on Him in the day of trouble, He will deliver them and they will honor Him.
psa-51-7-12: After his sin with Bathsheba, David asks God to wash him clean, create a pure heart in him, keep His Spirit with him and restore the joy of salvation.
psa-52-8-9: God's loving kindness is David's trust forever; he flourishes like a green olive tree in God's house and thanks Him for what He has done.
psa-54-4: God is David's helper, and the Lord sustains his life.
psa-55-22: God promises to sustain those who cast their burden on Him, and He will never let the righteous be moved.
psa-56-3-4: God's word is David's confidence; whenever he is afraid he trusts in God, and asks what mere flesh can do to him.
psa-56-8: God counts David's wanderings and keeps his tears as if in a bottle, recording them in His book.
psa-57-1: David pleads for God's mercy and takes refuge in the shadow of His wings until the disaster has passed.
psa-57-2-3: God Most High fulfills His purpose for David; He will send help from heaven and send out His loving kindness and truth.
psa-59-9-10: God is David's strength and high tower; His loving kindness goes before him and will let him see his enemies defeated.
psa-60-11-12: God, not human help, gives victory; through Him His people will do valiantly, for He will tread down their enemies.
psa-61-1-4: God has been David's refuge and strong tower, and from the ends of the earth David asks Him to lead him to the rock higher than he.
psa-62-1-2: God alone is David's rest, rock, salvation and fortress, so he will not be greatly shaken.
psa-62-5-8: God alone is the rock, salvation and refuge of His people, so they are urged to trust Him at all times and pour out their hearts before Him.
psa-63-1-4: God's loving kindness is better than life, so David, thirsting for Him in a dry land, will praise Him as long as he lives.
psa-64-10: God will be the joy and refuge of the righteous, and all the upright in heart will praise Him.
psa-65-1-4: God hears prayer and atones for sins that overwhelm His people; blessed is the one He chooses and brings near to dwell in His courts.
psa-66-8-9: God preserves His people's lives and does not let their feet slip, so all peoples are called to praise Him.
psa-66-16-20: God hears the prayer of the one who does not cherish sin in his heart, and He does not withdraw His loving kindness from those who call on Him.
psa-67-1-2: The psalm asks God to be merciful, bless His people and make His face shine on them, so His salvation will be known among all nations.
psa-68-5-6: God is a father to the fatherless and defender of widows; He sets the lonely in families and leads prisoners out with singing.
psa-68-19-20: God daily bears His people's burdens; He is a God of deliverance, and escape from death belongs to Him.
psa-69-13: David prays to God in His time of favor, asking Him to answer out of His abundant loving kindness and faithful salvation.
psa-69-32-33: God hears the needy and does not despise His captive people, so the humble rejoice and those who seek Him take heart.
psa-70-4-5: David asks God to make all who seek Him rejoice, and as one poor and needy, he begs his helper and deliverer to come quickly.
psa-71-5-6: God has been the psalmist's hope and confidence from youth, sustaining him since birth, so he will always praise Him.
psa-71-14-16: God's righteousness and saving acts are beyond measure, so the psalmist resolves to keep hoping and tell of them all day long.
psa-71-20-21: God, who has allowed His servant to see many bitter troubles, will restore his life, bring him up from the depths and comfort him again.
psa-72-12-14: God's ideal king delivers the needy who cry out, pities the poor and counts their lives precious, a reign Christians see fulfilled in Christ.
psa-72-17-19: God alone does marvelous deeds; the psalm prays that all nations be blessed through His king and that His glory fill the whole earth.
psa-73-23-26: God holds Asaph's hand, guides him with His counsel and will afterward receive him to glory; though his flesh fails, God is his strength and portion forever.
psa-73-28: God's nearness is Asaph's good, and he has made the Lord his refuge so he may tell of all His works.
psa-77-11-14: God's wonders of old are what Asaph resolves to remember in distress, for no god is as great as the God who works miracles.
psa-80-3: The psalm asks God to restore His people and make His face shine on them, so they will be saved.
psa-80-18-19: God's people pledge not to turn away from Him and ask the LORD of Armies to revive and restore them and make His face shine on them.
psa-81-10: God, who brought Israel out of Egypt, promises to fill their mouths if they open them wide, though the next verses lament that Israel would not listen.
psa-84-5-7: God promises blessing to those whose strength is in Him and whose hearts are set on seeking Him; even the valley of weeping becomes springs as they go from strength to strength.
psa-84-11-12: God promises to be a sun and shield, giving grace and glory and withholding no good thing from those who walk blamelessly; whoever trusts in Him is blessed.
psa-85-1-3: God showed favor to His land, restored Israel, forgave His people's iniquity, covered their sin and turned from His anger. That past mercy grounds hope for renewal.
psa-85-8-10: God promises to speak peace to His faithful people, who must not turn back to folly; His salvation is near those who fear Him, where mercy, truth, righteousness and peace meet.
psa-86-5: God is good, ready to forgive and abundant in loving kindness to all who call on Him.
psa-86-15: God is merciful and gracious, slow to anger and abundant in loving kindness and truth, as He revealed Himself to Moses.
psa-87-5-6: God promises to establish Zion and to record people from many nations as born there, counting them among His own people.
psa-89-1-4: God's loving kindness and faithfulness stand firm forever, and He swore to David to establish his offspring and throne for all generations.
psa-89-33-34: God promises that even when David's descendants are punished for sin, He will not remove His loving kindness, break His covenant or change His word.
psa-90-1-2: God has been His people's dwelling place in every generation; before the mountains or the earth were formed, He is God from everlasting to everlasting.
psa-90-12: Moses asks God to teach His people to number their days so they may gain a heart of wisdom.
psa-90-14: Moses asks God to satisfy His people each morning with His loving kindness, so they may rejoice and be glad all their days.
psa-91-1-4: God promises shelter to whoever dwells in His secret place and trusts Him as refuge: He will deliver from snares and deadly pestilence and cover them under His wings.
psa-91-5-8: God promises protection to those who trust Him, so they need not fear terror, arrows or plague; this speaks of His keeping care, not a guarantee of never suffering.
psa-91-9-13: God promises to guard those who make Him their refuge and dwelling place, giving His angels charge over them; it is trust, not a license to test God.
psa-91-14-16: God promises to deliver the one who loves Him and knows His name, to answer him, be with him in trouble, honor him and show him His salvation.
psa-92-1-2: God is worthy of thanks and praise, and it is good to declare His loving kindness each morning and His faithfulness each night.
psa-92-12-15: God promises that the righteous, planted in His house, will flourish like palm and cedar and still bear fruit in old age, showing that the LORD is upright.
psa-94-12-13: God promises that the person He disciplines and teaches from His law is blessed, and He gives them rest in days of trouble until the wicked are judged.
psa-94-14-15: God will not reject His people or forsake His inheritance; justice will return to righteousness, and the upright in heart will follow it.
psa-94-18-19: God's loving kindness upheld His servant when his foot was slipping, and His comfort brought joy amid anxious thoughts.
psa-96-11-13: God promises that He is coming to judge the earth, the world with righteousness and the peoples with His truth, so all creation is called to rejoice before Him.
psa-97-10-11: God promises to preserve the lives of His faithful people and deliver them from the wicked; those who love Him are called to hate evil, and light and gladness await the upright.
psa-98-1-3: God has worked salvation by His own power, revealed His righteousness to the nations and remembered His loving kindness to Israel, so all are called to sing a new song.
psa-99-8: God answered Moses, Aaron and Samuel when they called. He forgave His people, yet still disciplined their wrongdoing; His mercy and holiness go together.
psa-100-5: God is good. His loving kindness endures forever, and His faithfulness continues to all generations.
psa-102-17-20: God answers the prayer of the destitute and hears the groans of prisoners, and this is written so future generations will praise Him.
psa-102-25-28: God promises that, though heaven and earth wear out like clothing, He remains the same forever, and the children of His servants will be established before Him.
psa-103-1-5: God forgives all sin, heals diseases, redeems life from destruction, crowns it with loving kindness and satisfies with good things, so David calls himself to praise Him.
psa-103-8-12: God is merciful, gracious and slow to anger; He does not repay us as our sins deserve, but removes our transgressions as far as the east is from the west.
psa-103-13-14: God has compassion on those who fear Him like a father on his children, for He remembers that we are dust.
psa-103-17-18: God's loving kindness endures forever for those who fear Him, and His righteousness reaches their children's children who keep His covenant.
psa-105-8-11: God remembers His covenant forever, the oath He swore to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob to give Israel the land of Canaan as their inheritance.
psa-106-44-46: God still regarded rebellious Israel's distress when they cried out, remembered His covenant and made even their captors pity them.
psa-107-1-2: God is good and His loving kindness endures forever, so those He has redeemed from the hand of the enemy are called to give thanks and say so.
psa-107-13-16: When rebellious prisoners cried to God in their trouble, He saved them, brought them out of darkness and broke their chains, so they are called to praise His loving kindness.
psa-107-19-20: When people afflicted through their own foolishness cried to God in their trouble, He sent His word, healed them and delivered them from the grave.
psa-107-28-30: When sailors in a deadly storm cried to God in their trouble, He calmed the sea, stilled the waves and brought them to the harbor they longed for.
psa-108-12-13: God, not human help, gives victory; through Him His people will do valiantly, for He will tread down their enemies.
psa-110-1-4: God invites David's Lord to sit at His right hand until His enemies are subdued and swears he is a priest forever after Melchizedek, words fulfilled in Jesus.
psa-111-5: God provides food for those who fear Him, and He always remembers His covenant.
psa-111-9-10: God sent redemption to His people and established His covenant forever. His name is holy and awesome, and the fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom.
psa-112-1-4: God promises blessing to the one who fears Him and delights in His commandments: their descendants and righteousness endure, and light dawns in darkness for the upright.
psa-113-7-9: God raises the poor from the dust and the needy from the ash heap to sit with princes, and gives the childless woman a home as a joyful mother.
psa-115-11-13: God is the help and shield of those who fear Him; He remembers His people and will bless all who fear Him, both small and great.
psa-116-1-9: God heard His servant's cry when death surrounded him, delivered him from death, tears and stumbling, and let him walk before the LORD among the living.
psa-116-15: The death of God's faithful people is precious in His sight; He does not treat their lives or their dying lightly.
psa-118-5-6: God answered the psalmist's cry in distress and set him free; with the LORD on his side, he will not fear what anyone can do.
psa-118-8-9: Taking refuge in God is better than trusting people, even powerful rulers, because human help has limits that God does not.
psa-118-14-17: God is the strength, song and salvation of His people; shouts of victory fill the tents of the righteous, who live to declare His works.
psa-118-22-24: God made the stone the builders rejected into the cornerstone, a marvelous work of His; Jesus applied it to Himself as the rejected Messiah.
psa-119-9-11: A young person keeps their way pure by living according to God's word; hiding God's word in the heart guards against sinning against Him.
psa-119-28: The psalmist, weary with sorrow, asks God to strengthen him according to His word.
psa-119-49: God's word to His servant gives hope, and His servant asks Him to remember what He has spoken.
psa-119-50: God's word brings comfort in affliction and renewed life.
psa-119-67-68: God uses affliction to bring the straying back to His word. He is good and does good, and He teaches His statutes.
psa-119-71-72: God uses affliction to teach His statutes, and His instruction is worth more than thousands of pieces of gold and silver.
psa-119-76: God's loving kindness, according to His word, is the comfort His servant prays for.
psa-119-105: God's word is a lamp to the feet and a light for the path, showing the way forward and keeping His people from stumbling in the dark.
psa-119-114: God is a hiding place and shield; His word gives His people hope.
psa-119-116: In prayer, God's servant asks to be upheld according to His word, so that he may live and his hope in God will not be put to shame.
psa-119-165: God's word promises great peace to those who love His law; nothing causes them to stumble.
psa-120-1: God answered the psalmist when he cried to Him in distress.
psa-121-1-4: God, Maker of heaven and earth, is His people's help; He will not let their foot slip, and the One who keeps Israel never slumbers or sleeps.
psa-121-5-8: God promises to be His people's keeper and shade, guarding them day and night, keeping them from all evil and watching over their going out and coming in forever.
psa-124-6-8: God did not let Israel's enemies devour them; they escaped like a bird from a broken snare, for their help is in the name of the Maker of heaven and earth.
psa-125-1-2: God promises that those who trust Him are as secure as Mount Zion, which cannot be moved, and that He surrounds His people now and forever.
psa-126-5-6: God's restoring work means those who sow in tears will reap with joy, returning with songs and sheaves.
psa-127-1-2: God must build the house and guard the city or the work is in vain; anxious toil gains nothing, for He gives sleep to His beloved.
psa-127-3-5: Children are a heritage and reward from God. Like arrows in a warrior's hand, many children were a family's strength and honor in ancient Israel.
psa-128-1-4: God promises blessing to everyone who fears Him and walks in His ways, pictured as enjoying the fruit of their work and a fruitful family; it shows His favor, not a formula.
psa-130-1-2: Out of the depths, the psalmist cries to God and asks Him to hear his plea for mercy.
psa-130-3-5: No one could stand if God kept a record of sins, but with Him there is forgiveness, so He is feared and His word is worth waiting and hoping for.
psa-130-7-8: God promises that with Him is loving kindness and abundant redemption, and that He will redeem Israel from all their sins, so His people are called to hope in Him.
psa-131-1-3: God is the rest of a quieted soul, like a weaned child with its mother, and Israel is called to hope in the LORD forever.
psa-132-11-12: God swore to David that his descendants would sit on his throne, and that their line would continue forever if his children kept God's covenant.
psa-132-13-16: God promises that Zion is His chosen dwelling forever: He will bless her provision, satisfy her poor with bread, clothe her priests with salvation and fill her faithful with joy.
psa-133-1-3: God commands His blessing of life where His people live together in unity, which is as good and refreshing as anointing oil and the dew of Hermon.
psa-135-13-14: God promises that His name endures through all generations and that He will vindicate His people and have compassion on His servants, unlike idols that cannot act.
psa-136-1-3: God is good, the God of gods and Lord of lords, and His loving kindness endures forever.
psa-138-1-3: God answered David the day he called and strengthened his soul, so he thanks Him wholeheartedly for His loving kindness and truth.
psa-138-7-8: God will revive David in the midst of trouble, save him with His right hand and fulfill His purpose for him, for His loving kindness endures forever.
psa-139-1-6: God knows David completely, his actions, thoughts and every word before he speaks, a knowledge too wonderful for him to grasp.
psa-139-7-12: God's presence reaches everywhere, from heaven to the grave to the farthest sea, and even darkness is not dark to Him.
psa-139-13-16: God formed David in his mother's womb, fearfully and wonderfully, and wrote all his days in His book before one of them came to be.
psa-139-23-24: David asks God to search his heart, test his thoughts, reveal any wicked way in him and lead him in the everlasting way.
psa-140-12-13: God will maintain the cause of the afflicted and justice for the needy, and the upright will dwell in His presence.
psa-141-1-2: David asks God to come quickly and receive his prayer like incense and his lifted hands like the evening sacrifice.
psa-142-1-5: God knows David's way when his spirit is overwhelmed and no one cares for him; he cries out that the LORD is his refuge and portion.
psa-143-8-10: David asks God to let him hear His loving kindness each morning, show him the way to walk, rescue him and teach him by His good Spirit to do His will.
psa-144-1-2: God is David's rock, who trains his hands for battle, and his loving kindness, fortress, deliverer and shield.
psa-144-15: God's people are truly happy; blessed are the people whose God is the LORD.
psa-145-8-9: God is gracious, merciful, slow to anger and great in loving kindness; He is good to all and His mercies are over all His works.
psa-145-13-16: God's kingdom is everlasting and He is faithful in all His words; He upholds all who fall and gives every living thing its food in due season.
psa-145-17-20: God is near to all who call on Him in truth; He fulfills the desire of those who fear Him, hears their cry and saves them.
psa-146-5-9: God, the Creator who keeps faith forever, brings justice to the oppressed, feeds the hungry, frees prisoners and upholds foreigners, orphans and widows.
psa-147-3: God promises to heal the brokenhearted and bind up their wounds, as He did when gathering Jerusalem's exiles.
psa-147-11: God takes pleasure not in human strength but in those who fear Him and hope in His loving kindness.
psa-149-4: God takes pleasure in His people and promises to crown the humble with salvation.
pro-1-7: Proverbs opens with its key idea: reverence for the LORD is the starting point of true knowledge. Only fools reject wisdom and correction.
pro-1-23: Wisdom, pictured as a woman calling in the streets, urges the careless to respond to her warning. If they turn, she will pour out her thoughts and make her teaching known to them.
pro-1-33: Ending her warning to those who ignore her, Wisdom says that whoever listens to her will live in safety and be free from the dread of disaster.
pro-2-6-8: A father tells his son that wisdom is God's gift. The LORD stores up sound judgment for the upright, shields those with integrity and guards the way of his faithful people.
pro-3-1-2: A father urges his son not to forget his teaching but keep it in his heart. Living this way generally brings long life and peace, though Proverbs offers principles rather than guarantees.
pro-3-5-6: A father urges his son to rely fully on God rather than his own judgment, and to honour God in every part of life. It is a wisdom principle: God guides those who trust him, but no easy path is guaranteed.
pro-3-7-8: The father warns his son against thinking himself wise. Revering the LORD and turning from evil brings a healthy, whole life, as a general rule of wisdom.
pro-3-9-10: The father tells his son to honour the LORD with the first and best of his produce. In Israel's farming world this was linked with full barns, describing God's usual blessing, not a payment scheme.
pro-3-11-12: The father urges his son not to resent the LORD's correction, because God disciplines those he loves, as a father corrects a son he delights in. Hebrews 12 quotes this.
pro-3-13-18: The father says the person who finds wisdom is blessed, since she is worth more than silver, gold or jewels. Wisdom brings long life, honour, pleasant ways and peace, like a tree of life.
pro-3-21-26: The father tells his son to hold on to sound judgment, which brings life and a secure walk. He can sleep without fear, because the LORD will be his confidence and keep him from traps.
pro-4-5-7: A father urges his son to make getting wisdom his priority, whatever it costs. If he loves and holds on to wisdom, it will protect and guard him.
pro-4-18: The father compares the life of the righteous to the dawn, which grows brighter and brighter until full day. In contrast, the way of the wicked is deep darkness.
pro-4-20-22: A father asks his son to pay close attention to his words and keep them in his heart, because wise teaching brings life and wholeness to those who take hold of it.
pro-6-20-23: The father urges his son to keep his parents' teaching close. It will guide him when he walks, guard him when he sleeps and speak to him when he wakes, like a lamp.
pro-8-17: Wisdom, speaking as a person, says she loves those who love her, and those who look for her earnestly will find her. Seeking wisdom is never wasted effort.
pro-8-32-35: Wisdom calls her listeners to heed her and keep her ways, waiting at her door daily. Whoever finds her finds life and receives favour from the LORD.
pro-9-10-11: Proverbs repeats that reverence for the LORD is the beginning of wisdom, and knowing the Holy One is real understanding. Wisdom says she adds years to life.
pro-10-3: This proverb observes that the LORD does not let the righteous starve but frustrates the cravings of the wicked. It describes God's general care, not a promise against every hardship.
pro-10-12: This proverb contrasts hatred, which stirs up conflict, with love, which covers over offences instead of exposing them. Peter quotes this in urging Christians to love one another.
pro-10-22: Solomon observes that the LORD's blessing makes people rich without adding the sorrow that often comes with wealth gained by toil and greed.
pro-11-2: This proverb warns that pride leads to disgrace, while humility goes hand in hand with wisdom.
pro-11-24-25: Solomon notes a paradox: generous people often end up with more, while stingy people end up in need. Those who refresh others will themselves be refreshed.
pro-12-25: This proverb observes that anxiety weighs a person down, but a kind and encouraging word can lift their heart.
pro-13-12: Solomon observes that hope that keeps being delayed makes a person sick at heart, but a longing finally fulfilled brings new life, like a tree of life.
pro-14-26-27: This proverb says that revering the LORD gives a person strong security and a refuge for their children. It is like a fountain of life that turns people away from deadly traps.
pro-15-1: This proverb teaches that a gentle reply can calm anger, while harsh words stir it up. How we answer often decides whether conflict grows.
pro-15-13: Solomon observes that a happy heart shows on the face, while heartache crushes the spirit. Our inner state affects our whole life.
pro-15-29: This proverb says the LORD keeps his distance from the wicked but listens to the prayers of those who live rightly.
pro-16-3: This proverb advises entrusting all our work to the LORD. Plans made in dependence on God tend to stand, though Proverbs also says God decides the final outcome.
pro-16-7: Solomon observes that when a person's life pleases the LORD, God can even turn enemies toward peace with them. It is a general pattern, not a promise of no opposition.
pro-16-9: This proverb notes that people make their plans, but it is the LORD who determines their steps. Planning is wise, but God has the final say.
pro-18-10: This proverb pictures the LORD's name as a strong tower. The righteous run to him and are safe, in contrast to the rich, who trust in their wealth.
pro-18-14: Solomon observes that a healthy spirit can carry a person through illness, but a crushed spirit is almost impossible to bear.
pro-18-24: This proverb warns that having many casual companions can lead to ruin, but a true friend can be more loyal than a brother.
pro-19-17: Solomon teaches that kindness to the poor is like lending to the LORD himself, and God will repay what was given.
pro-19-21: This proverb observes that people may have many plans, but it is the LORD's purpose that finally stands.
pro-19-23: Solomon says that revering the LORD leads to life, so a person can rest content and untouched by harm. It describes the general fruit of reverence, not immunity from trouble.
pro-20-22: This proverb warns against taking revenge. Instead, wait for the LORD, and he will bring deliverance. Paul echoes this in Romans 12.
pro-21-5: Solomon contrasts careful, diligent planning, which tends to bring gain, with hasty shortcuts, which usually lead to poverty.
pro-21-30-31: This proverb says no human wisdom or plan can succeed against the LORD. People prepare horses for battle, but victory belongs to God.
pro-22-4: Solomon observes that humility and reverence for the LORD tend to bring riches, honour and life. This is the normal pattern of wisdom, not a promise of wealth.
pro-22-6: This proverb encourages parents to train a child in the way they should go, since early training usually shapes the whole of life. It is a principle, not a promise that every child will follow.
pro-24-13-14: Just as honey is sweet and good, the writer tells his son, wisdom is good for the soul. If he finds it, he will have a future, and his hope will not be cut off.
pro-24-16: This proverb says the righteous may fall many times and still get up again, while the wicked are brought down by disaster. It warns those who plot against the godly.
pro-28-13: This proverb teaches that hiding our sins leads nowhere good, but confessing and turning away from them brings mercy.
pro-29-25: Solomon warns that fear of what people think becomes a trap, but whoever trusts in the LORD is kept safe.
pro-30-5: Agur, a wisdom teacher, says every word of God is pure and proven true. God shields those who take refuge in him, so nothing should be added to his words.
ecc-3-11: The Teacher reflects that God makes everything beautiful in its proper time. He has put a sense of eternity in human hearts, yet people cannot grasp all that God is doing.
ecc-3-14: The Teacher concludes that what God does lasts for ever; nothing can be added or taken away. God acts this way so people will stand in awe of him.
ecc-5-19-20: The Teacher says the ability to enjoy wealth, work and life is itself a gift from God. Those given that joy are kept so busy with gladness that they do not brood over life's brevity.
ecc-12-13-14: The Teacher sums up the whole book: revere God and keep his commands, because this is everyone's duty. God will judge every deed, including hidden ones, good or evil.
isa-1-18: After accusing Judah of corruption, God invites them to settle the matter with him. Sins stained deep red can be washed white as snow, if they are willing to obey.
isa-2-2-4: Isaiah foresees a day when the nations stream to the LORD's temple to learn his ways. God will settle disputes, and people will turn weapons into farming tools and stop training for war.
isa-4-5-6: Isaiah promised that after cleansing Jerusalem, God would cover Zion with cloud by day and fire by night, as in the exodus. His glory would be a shelter from heat and storm.
isa-6-6-7: In Isaiah's vision, after he confessed his unclean lips, a seraph touched his mouth with a burning coal from the altar and declared his guilt removed and his sin forgiven.
isa-7-14: Isaiah told faithless King Ahaz that God would give a sign: a young woman would bear a son named Immanuel, "God with us". Matthew sees the full meaning in Jesus' birth to the virgin Mary.
isa-9-2: Isaiah foretold that people living in darkness and under the shadow of death would see a great light. Matthew applies this to Jesus' ministry in Galilee.
isa-9-6-7: Isaiah foretold the birth of a royal child with names like Wonderful Counsellor, Mighty God and Prince of Peace. His just reign on David's throne would grow without end; Christians see this fulfilled in Jesus.
isa-10-20-21: Isaiah foretold that after Assyria's attack, a remnant of Israel would stop relying on the power that struck them and truly rely on the LORD, the Holy One of Israel, returning to the mighty God.
isa-11-1-5: Isaiah foretold that a new shoot would grow from the stump of Jesse's family. The LORD's Spirit would rest on this king, who would judge the poor fairly and rule with righteousness. Christians see Jesus here.
isa-11-6-9: Isaiah pictures the Messiah's reign as a world where wolves live with lambs and children play safely near snakes. No harm will be done, for the earth will be full of the knowledge of the LORD.
isa-12-1-2: Isaiah gives the rescued people a song for that future day: God's anger has turned to comfort. They will trust him without fear, because the LORD is their strength, song and salvation.
isa-12-3: Isaiah tells the restored people that they will joyfully draw water from the wells of salvation, an image of drinking deeply from God's rescue as from a spring.
isa-14-1-2: Isaiah promised that after Babylon fell, the LORD would again show compassion on Israel, choose them, settle them in their land and draw foreigners to join them.
isa-25-6-8: Isaiah foresees God preparing a rich feast for all peoples on his mountain. He will remove the shroud of death, swallow up death for ever and wipe away every tear. Paul and Revelation echo this.
isa-26-3-4: In a song for the day of salvation, God's people declare that he keeps in perfect peace those whose minds rest on him because they trust him. The LORD is a rock that lasts for ever.
isa-26-12: Judah's song tells the LORD that he will establish peace for them, since everything they have accomplished has really been his work.
isa-26-19: Against the despair of death, Isaiah declares that God's dead will live and their bodies rise. Those in the dust are called to wake and sing, one of the Old Testament's clearest hopes of resurrection.
isa-28-16: Against leaders who trusted a deal with death, God promised to lay a tested, precious cornerstone in Zion. Whoever relies on it will not panic. Peter and Paul apply this to Christ.
isa-29-18-19: Isaiah foretold a day when the deaf would hear God's word and the blind see. The humble and poor would rejoice in the Holy One of Israel, while oppressors disappear.
isa-30-15: God told Judah that their safety lay in turning back to him and resting, and their strength in quiet trust. Instead they refused and looked to Egypt's horses for help.
isa-30-18: Despite Judah's stubbornness, Isaiah says the LORD waits to be gracious and rises to show them mercy. He is a God of justice, and those who wait for him are blessed.
isa-30-19-21: Isaiah promised Zion that God would answer as soon as they cried out. Even after hard times, their teacher would no longer hide, and a voice would guide them: this is the way.
isa-32-1-2: Isaiah foresees a king who reigns justly and rulers who govern fairly. Each would be like a shelter from wind and storm, streams in a desert and shade from a great rock.
isa-32-17-18: Isaiah foresees that when God's Spirit is poured out, righteousness will produce peace, quiet and lasting confidence. God's people will live in secure and peaceful homes.
isa-33-2: Facing the Assyrian threat, Isaiah prays for God's grace on his people who wait for him. He asks God to be their strength every morning and their rescue in trouble.
isa-33-5-6: Isaiah praises the LORD, exalted on high, who fills Zion with justice. He will be the stable foundation of their times, a rich store of salvation and wisdom; reverence for him is their treasure.
isa-35-1-2: Isaiah pictures the desert bursting into bloom and singing for joy. The dry land will receive the beauty of Lebanon and Carmel, and people will see the glory of the LORD.
isa-35-3-4: Isaiah tells God's people to strengthen weak hands and shaky knees, and to tell the fearful to take courage, because their God is coming to judge their enemies and save them.
isa-35-5-6: Isaiah foretells that when God comes, the blind will see, the deaf hear, the lame leap and the mute sing, while streams flow in the desert. Jesus pointed to his miracles as fulfilling this.
isa-35-8-10: Isaiah foresees a highway called the Way of Holiness, safe from wild animals, on which God's redeemed will return to Zion singing. Joy will overtake them, and sorrow will flee.
isa-38-16-17: After recovering from a deadly illness, King Hezekiah thanks God for restoring his life. He sees that his bitter suffering was for his good, because God in love saved him and put his sins behind his back.
isa-40-1-2: God tells his prophets to comfort his people and speak tenderly to Jerusalem: her hard service is over and her sin has been paid for. It opens Isaiah's message of hope to the exiles.
isa-40-4-5: A voice calls for a road to be prepared for God, with valleys raised and mountains levelled. Then God's glory will be revealed for all to see. The Gospels apply this to John the Baptist.
isa-40-8: Isaiah contrasts human life, which withers like grass and fades like flowers, with God's word, which stands for ever. What God has spoken can be relied on completely.
isa-40-10-11: Isaiah announces that the Sovereign LORD comes with power, yet he cares for his people like a shepherd. He gathers the lambs in his arms and gently leads those with young.
isa-40-28-31: Isaiah reminded weary Israel that the eternal Creator never tires and gives strength to the weak. Those who wait for the LORD will find fresh strength to keep going, a truth still offered to God's people.
isa-41-8-10: God promised Israel, whom he had chosen as his servant, that they need not fear, because he was with them. He would strengthen and help them and hold them up with his righteous right hand.
isa-41-13-14: God promised weak and despised Israel, whom he calls a worm, that he would hold their right hand and help them. He is their Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel.
isa-41-17-18: God promised that when the poor and needy search for water and find none, he would answer and not abandon them. He would open rivers on barren hills and springs in valleys.
isa-42-1-4: God introduces his chosen servant, filled with his Spirit, who will bring justice to the nations gently, without shouting or breaking a bruised reed. Matthew applies this to Jesus.
isa-42-6-7: God tells his servant that he has called and will keep him, to be a covenant for the people and a light for the nations, opening blind eyes and freeing prisoners.
isa-42-16: God promised to lead his blind and helpless people along unfamiliar paths, turning darkness into light and rough places into smooth ground. He would do this and not abandon them.
isa-43-1-2: God told Israel not to fear, because he had created and redeemed them and called them by name. When they passed through deep waters or fire, he would be with them, and they would not be destroyed.
isa-43-4-5: God told Israel they were precious and honoured in his sight and that he loved them. He promised to be with them and gather their scattered descendants from east and west.
isa-43-10-11: God calls Israel to be his witnesses, so they would know and believe that he alone is God. No god came before him or will come after him, and apart from him there is no saviour.
isa-43-18-19: God told the exiles not to dwell only on the past exodus, because he was doing something new: making a road through the wilderness and rivers in the desert to bring them home.
isa-43-25: Although Israel had burdened him with their sins, God declared that he himself wipes out their wrongdoing for his own sake and will not remember their sins.
isa-44-2-3: God, who formed Israel, told his chosen people not to be afraid. He promised to pour water on thirsty land and his Spirit and blessing on their descendants.
isa-44-21-22: God reminds Israel that he formed them and will not forget them. He has already swept away their sins like a cloud, so he calls them to return to him, because he has redeemed them.
isa-45-2-3: God promised Cyrus, the Persian king who would free the exiles, that he would go before him, break down gates and give him hidden treasures, so Cyrus would know who called him.
isa-45-5-6: God declares to Cyrus that he is the LORD and there is no other god. He equipped Cyrus, though Cyrus did not know him, so the whole world would recognise that God alone is God.
isa-45-22: God calls people from every corner of the earth to turn to him and be saved, because he is God and there is no other. Rescue is offered to every nation, not only Israel.
isa-46-3-4: Unlike idols that must be carried, God reminded Israel that he had carried them from birth. He promised to keep carrying and sustaining them into old age and grey hair.
isa-48-10-11: God tells Israel that he has refined them in the furnace of suffering, not to destroy them but to test them. He acts for the sake of his own name and will not give his glory to another.
isa-48-17-18: God, their Redeemer, reminds Israel that he teaches them what is good and leads them in the right way. He laments that had they obeyed, their peace would have flowed like a river.
isa-49-6: God tells his servant that restoring Israel is too small a task; he will also be a light to the nations, bringing God's salvation to the ends of the earth. Paul and Simeon applied this to Christ's mission.
isa-49-8-10: God promised his servant help in the day of salvation, to restore the land and set prisoners free. The returning people would not hunger or thirst, because God would lead them to springs.
isa-49-13: Isaiah calls the heavens, earth and mountains to burst into song, because the LORD has comforted his people and will show compassion to those who suffer.
isa-49-14-16: When Zion complained that God had forgotten her, God answered that even if a mother forgot her baby, he would never forget her. Her name is engraved on his hands.
isa-49-24-26: To exiles who doubted that captives could be rescued from a powerful enemy, God promised that he himself would fight their oppressors and free their children.
isa-50-4-5: God's servant says the Lord has taught him how to speak words that sustain the weary. Every morning he listens to God, and he has not rebelled or turned away.
isa-50-7-9: Facing abuse, God's servant sets his face like flint, confident that God will help him and prove him right. No accuser can condemn him, because the Lord defends him.
isa-51-3: Isaiah promised that the LORD would comfort Zion and turn her ruins and deserts into a garden like Eden. Joy, gladness, thanksgiving and song would fill the land again.
isa-51-6: God tells his people to look at the sky and earth, which will one day vanish like smoke and wear out like clothes. But his salvation lasts for ever and his righteousness will never fail.
isa-51-11: Isaiah foretells that those the LORD has rescued will return to Zion singing, crowned with everlasting joy. Gladness will overtake them, and sorrow and sighing will run away.
isa-51-12: God reminds his fearful people that he himself is the one who comforts them. Why fear mere humans, who die like grass, and forget the LORD who made them?
isa-52-6-7: God says his people will know that he is the one speaking. Isaiah pictures a messenger crossing the mountains with good news of peace and salvation, announcing to Zion that her God reigns.
isa-52-9-10: Isaiah calls Jerusalem's ruins to break into song, because God has comforted and redeemed his people. He has shown his power before every nation, and all the earth will see his salvation.
isa-53-4-6: Isaiah describes the suffering servant who carried our pain and was pierced for our wrongdoing. We had all wandered like sheep, and God laid our guilt on him. The New Testament sees this as Jesus' death.
isa-53-10-11: Isaiah says it was God's will for the servant to suffer as an offering for sin. Afterward he would see life and be satisfied, and by his knowledge he would make many righteous by bearing their sins.
isa-54-4-5: God told Zion, pictured as a shamed and abandoned wife, not to fear disgrace. Her Maker would be her husband, and her Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel, God of all the earth.
isa-54-7-8: God told Zion that he had left her only for a brief moment in his anger, but would bring her back with great compassion and everlasting love.
isa-54-10: God promised Zion that even if mountains were shaken and hills removed, his unfailing love and his covenant of peace with her would never be taken away.
isa-54-11-13: God promised storm-battered, uncomforted Zion that he would rebuild her with precious stones. All her children would be taught by the LORD and enjoy great peace.
isa-54-14-17: God promised restored Zion that she would be established in righteousness and far from terror. No weapon formed against her would succeed; this is the heritage of the LORD's servants.
isa-55-1-2: God calls everyone who is thirsty to come and receive water, wine and milk free of charge. He asks why people spend their money and effort on what cannot satisfy.
isa-55-3: God urges his people to listen and come to him so that they may live. He offers an everlasting covenant based on his faithful love promised to David. Paul links this to Jesus' resurrection.
isa-55-6-7: Isaiah urges people to seek the LORD while he can be found. If the wicked abandon their ways and thoughts and return to God, he will show mercy and forgive them generously.
isa-55-8-9: God says his thoughts and ways are not like ours. As the heavens are higher than the earth, his ways are higher, which is why his mercy can exceed what we expect.
isa-55-10-11: God compares his word to rain and snow that water the earth and make it fruitful. What he speaks will not return empty but will accomplish what he intends.
isa-55-12-13: God promised the exiles that they would leave Babylon with joy and be led home in peace. Mountains and trees would celebrate, and thorns would give way to cypress and myrtle.
isa-56-3-5: God told foreigners and eunuchs who held to his covenant not to think themselves excluded. He would give them a place and a name in his house, better than sons and daughters.
isa-56-6-7: God promised that foreigners who love and serve him would be brought to his holy mountain and given joy in his house, which would be called a house of prayer for all nations.
isa-57-15: The high and holy God says he lives in eternity, yet also with those who are humble and sorry for their sin. He comes close to revive their spirits and hearts.
