isa-57-18-19: God says he has seen his people's stubborn ways, yet he will heal them, guide them and comfort their mourners. He offers peace to those far and near.
isa-58-6-8: God tells Judah that the fast he wants is justice: freeing the oppressed, feeding the hungry and sheltering the poor. Then their light would break out like dawn and healing would come quickly.
isa-58-9-11: God promised Judah that if they stopped oppression and accusation and cared for the hungry, he would answer their prayers, guide them always and make them like a well-watered garden.
isa-59-1: Isaiah tells Judah that God's arm is not too weak to save, nor his ear too dull to hear. The real barrier is their sin, which has separated them from him.
isa-59-20-21: God promised that a Redeemer would come to Zion for those who turn from sin. His covenant was that his Spirit and words would stay with them and their descendants for ever. Paul quotes this.
isa-60-1-3: God calls Zion to rise and shine, because his glory has dawned on her while darkness covers the earth. Nations and kings will be drawn to her light.
isa-60-19-20: God promised that Zion would no longer need sun or moon, because the LORD himself would be her everlasting light, and her days of mourning would end. Revelation echoes this.
isa-61-1-3: The Spirit-anointed messenger announces good news to the poor, healing for the brokenhearted and freedom for captives, and gives mourners joy instead of ashes. Jesus said this was fulfilled in him.
isa-61-7-8: God promised his shamed people a double portion and everlasting joy instead of disgrace. Because he loves justice and hates robbery, he would reward them faithfully and make an everlasting covenant.
isa-61-10-11: Zion rejoices that God has clothed her in salvation and righteousness like a bride or bridegroom in wedding clothes. As a garden makes seeds grow, God will make righteousness spring up.
isa-62-2-4: God promised Zion a new name: no longer Deserted or Desolate, but My Delight Is in Her. The nations would see her glory, and God would take joy in her as a bridegroom in his bride.
isa-62-11-12: God proclaims to the ends of the earth that Zion's salvation is coming. Her people will be called the Holy People and the Redeemed, and the city Sought After, no longer forsaken.
isa-63-7-9: Isaiah recalls God's many kindnesses to Israel. In all their distress he too was distressed, and in his love and mercy he rescued them and carried them through the days of old.
isa-64-4-5: In a prayer of the people, Isaiah says no one has ever seen a God like the LORD, who acts for those who wait for him. He meets those who gladly do right, though the people confess their sin.
isa-65-17-19: God announces that he will create new heavens and a new earth, and make Jerusalem a source of joy. The sound of weeping will no longer be heard there. Revelation develops this vision.
isa-65-24: In his picture of the new creation, God says he will answer his people before they even call and hear them while they are still speaking.
isa-66-12-13: God promised to give Jerusalem peace flowing like a river. As a mother comforts her child, he would comfort his people.
isa-66-22: God promised that just as the new heavens and new earth he will make will last, so his people's descendants and name will endure before him.
jer-1-5: Jeremiah recounts God's call: before he was formed in the womb, God knew him and set him apart to be a prophet to the nations. His calling came before his birth.
jer-1-7-8: When Jeremiah protested that he was too young, God told him to go wherever he was sent and say whatever he was told. He need not fear, because God would be with him to rescue him.
jer-1-19: God warned Jeremiah that kings, priests and people would fight against him, but promised they would not overcome him, because God would be with him to rescue him.
jer-3-12-14: God sent Jeremiah to call unfaithful Israel to return. He would not stay angry for ever, because he is merciful; they only had to admit their guilt and come back to him.
jer-3-15: God promised returning Israel that he would give them shepherds after his own heart, leaders who would feed them with knowledge and understanding.
jer-6-16: God urged Judah to stop at the crossroads and ask for the old, good way, and walk in it to find rest for their souls. Sadly, the people refused.
jer-7-23: God reminds Judah that what he really commanded their ancestors was not sacrifices but obedience: listen to him, and he would be their God and they his people, and it would go well with them.
jer-9-23-24: God tells people not to boast about their wisdom, strength or wealth. If anyone boasts, let it be about knowing God, who delights in kindness, justice and righteousness.
jer-11-4: God reminds Judah of the covenant he made when he brought their ancestors out of Egypt's iron furnace: obey me, and you will be my people and I will be your God.
jer-15-19-20: When Jeremiah complained bitterly, God told him to repent and speak worthy words. If he did, God would make him a fortified wall that enemies could not overcome.
jer-16-14-15: God promised that a day would come when Israel would remember him less for the exodus from Egypt and more for bringing them back from the north and all the lands of exile.
jer-17-7-8: God says that the person who trusts in the LORD is blessed, like a tree planted by water. Its roots reach the stream, so it stays green and fruitful even in drought.
jer-17-9-10: Jeremiah observes that the human heart is deceitful beyond understanding. God answers that he searches every heart and mind and will repay each person according to their deeds.
jer-23-3-4: After condemning Judah's bad leaders, God promised to gather the scattered remnant of his flock and give them good shepherds, so they would no longer be afraid or lost.
jer-23-5-6: God promised to raise up a righteous Branch from David's line, a wise king who would do justice. He would be called "The LORD Our Righteousness". Christians see this fulfilled in Jesus.
jer-24-6-7: In the vision of good figs, God promised the exiles that he would watch over them, bring them home and give them a heart to know him. They would be his people.
jer-29-10-11: God promised the exiles in Babylon that after seventy years he would bring them home. His plans for them were for their welfare and a hopeful future, though the exile would not end quickly.
jer-29-12-14: God told the exiles that when they prayed and sought him with all their heart, they would find him. He would then restore their fortunes and gather them home from the nations.
jer-30-8-10: God promised to break the yoke of foreign oppression from his people's necks. They would serve him and a king from David's line, and need not fear, because he would save them.
jer-30-17: God promised to restore Zion's health and heal her wounds, because others had called her an outcast that no one cared about.
jer-30-18-22: God promised to restore Jacob's homes and rebuild Jerusalem on its ruins. Songs of thanks would rise, their numbers would grow, and they would be his people and he their God.
jer-31-3: Israel recalls God's message: he has loved them with an everlasting love and drawn them to himself with unfailing kindness. His love is the reason he will restore them.
jer-31-8-9: God promised to bring his people home from the far north, including the blind, the lame and pregnant women. They would return weeping and praying, and he would lead them like a father.
jer-31-12-14: God promised that the returned exiles would sing on Zion and enjoy grain, wine, oil and flocks. Their lives would be like a watered garden, and their mourning would turn to joy.
jer-31-16-17: God told Rachel, weeping for her lost children, to stop crying. Her children would return from the enemy's land, so there was hope for her future.
jer-31-20: God calls Ephraim his dear son. Even when he speaks against him, he still remembers him and his heart yearns for him, so he will surely have mercy on him.
jer-31-25: God promised that he would refresh the weary and satisfy everyone who is faint with sorrow when he restored his people.
jer-31-31-34: God promised a new covenant: he would write his law on his people's hearts, all would know him, and he would forgive their sins completely. Hebrews says Jesus brings this covenant.
jer-32-17: Imprisoned during the siege, Jeremiah prays after obeying God's command to buy a field. He confesses that the God who made heaven and earth finds nothing too hard.
jer-32-27: God answers Jeremiah's prayer by echoing it: he is the LORD, God of all humankind, so nothing is too hard for him, including bringing his people back to the land.
jer-32-37-41: God promised to gather his people from exile, let them live in safety and give them one heart to revere him. He would make an everlasting covenant and rejoice in doing them good.
jer-33-3: While Jeremiah was confined, God invited him to call on him and promised to answer, revealing great and hidden things he did not know about Jerusalem's future restoration.
jer-33-6-9: God promised to heal Jerusalem, restore Judah and Israel, cleanse them from sin and forgive them. The city would bring him joy and praise before all nations.
jer-33-10-11: God promised that in the deserted streets of Jerusalem there would again be sounds of joy, weddings and people bringing thank offerings to the temple.
jer-33-14-16: God promised to fulfil his good word by raising up a righteous Branch from David who would do justice. Judah would be saved and Jerusalem would live in safety.
jer-33-20-22: God said his covenant with David was as firm as his covenant with day and night. It could not be broken, and he would greatly increase David's descendants and the Levites.
jer-39-17-18: God promised Ebed-Melech, the Cushite official who rescued Jeremiah from the cistern, that he would be spared when Jerusalem fell, because he had trusted in the LORD.
jer-42-10-12: After Jerusalem's fall, God promised the survivors that if they stayed in the land rather than flee to Egypt, he would build them up and protect them from Babylon. They refused and went anyway.
jer-46-27-28: Amid judgments on the nations, God told Israel not to fear: he would bring their descendants back from captivity to peace. He would discipline them justly but never destroy them completely.
jer-50-4-5: God foretold that after Babylon fell, Israel and Judah would return together, weeping as they sought the LORD, and bind themselves to him in a covenant never to be forgotten.
jer-50-19-20: God promised to bring Israel back to its rich pastures. When the remnant he spared was searched for guilt, none would be found, because he would forgive them.
lam-3-21-23: In the middle of grief over Jerusalem's destruction, the poet finds hope by remembering that God's steadfast love keeps us from being consumed. His mercies are new every morning.
lam-3-24-26: The grieving poet declares that the LORD is all he has, so he will hope in him. God is good to those who seek him, and it is good to wait quietly for his rescue.
lam-3-31-33: The poet reasons that the Lord does not reject anyone for ever. Though he brings grief, he will show compassion, because he takes no pleasure in causing people pain.
lam-3-55-58: The poet remembers calling to God from the depths of a pit. God heard him, came near and said, "Do not fear." The Lord took up his case and redeemed his life.
ezk-11-19-20: God promised the exiles a single, undivided heart and a new spirit. He would replace their stony hearts with hearts of flesh so they would obey him and be his people.
ezk-16-60-63: After describing Jerusalem's unfaithfulness, God promised to remember his covenant and make an everlasting one with her. Forgiven, she would be ashamed of her past and know that he is the LORD.
ezk-18-21-23: God declared that if a wicked person turns from sin and does what is right, he will live, and his past offences will not be held against him. God takes no pleasure in anyone's death.
ezk-18-30-32: God warns Israel that he will judge each by their ways, and urges them to repent and get a new heart and spirit. He takes no pleasure in anyone's death, so he pleads: turn and live.
ezk-20-41-44: God promised that when he gathered Israel from the nations, he would accept them like a pleasing offering. Remembering their past, they would loathe their sins and know he dealt with them for his name's sake.
ezk-28-25-26: God promised that after gathering Israel from the nations, they would live securely in their land, build houses and plant vineyards, while he judged the neighbours who had scorned them.
ezk-34-11-12: Having condemned Israel's selfish leaders, God promised that he himself would search for his scattered sheep and rescue them from wherever they were scattered on a dark and cloudy day.
ezk-34-13-15: God promised to bring his flock home and feed them in good pastures on Israel's mountains. He himself would be their shepherd and make them lie down in safety.
ezk-34-16: God promised to seek the lost, bring back the strays, bandage the injured and strengthen the weak. But the fat and strong who had exploited the flock would face his justice.
ezk-34-22-24: God promised to rescue his flock and judge between sheep. He would set over them one shepherd, his servant David, a future king from David's line. Christians see this fulfilled in Jesus.
ezk-34-25-26: God promised his restored people a covenant of peace: wild beasts would be removed so they could sleep safely even in forests, and he would send showers of blessing in season.
ezk-34-27-28: God promised that the land would yield its crops and his people would live securely. When he broke their yoke of slavery, they would no longer be plundered and no one would make them afraid.
ezk-34-30-31: God concludes that his people would know he was with them and that they were his people. They are the sheep of his pasture, and he is their God.
ezk-36-9-11: God spoke to the mountains of Israel, declaring that he was for them. The land would again be farmed, its towns rebuilt and filled with people, and he would do more good than before.
ezk-36-24-25: God promised to gather Israel from all nations and bring them home. He would sprinkle clean water on them and cleanse them from all their impurity and idols.
ezk-36-26-28: God promised Israel a new heart and a new spirit, replacing their heart of stone with one of flesh. He would put his own Spirit in them so they would obey him and be his people.
ezk-36-29-30: God promised to save Israel from all uncleanness and to make grain and fruit plentiful, so they would never again suffer the disgrace of famine among the nations.
ezk-36-33-36: God promised that when he cleansed Israel from sin, their ruined cities would be rebuilt and the desolate land would become like Eden. The nations would know the LORD had done it.
ezk-37-5-6: In Ezekiel's vision of a valley of dry bones, God declares he will put breath, muscle and skin on them so they live. It pictured Israel's hopeless exiles being brought back to life as a nation.
ezk-37-12-14: Explaining the vision, God told the exiles, who felt dead and hopeless, that he would open their graves, put his Spirit in them so they would live, and settle them in their own land.
ezk-37-21-23: God promised to gather Israel from the nations and make them one nation under one king, no longer divided. He would cleanse them from their idols and they would be his people.
ezk-37-24-27: God promised that his servant David would be their one shepherd-king. He would make an everlasting covenant of peace and place his sanctuary among them for ever. Christians see this fulfilled in Christ.
ezk-39-25-29: God promised to restore Israel and have mercy on them. They would live safely, remembering their shame, and he would no longer hide his face, having poured out his Spirit on them.
ezk-47-8-9: In Ezekiel's temple vision, a guide shows him a river flowing from the temple into the Dead Sea. Its water makes the salt sea fresh, and life swarms wherever it goes.
ezk-47-12: The guide tells Ezekiel that fruit trees will grow on both banks of the temple river, bearing fruit every month and leaves that heal. Revelation 22 uses the same picture.
dan-2-20-22: After God revealed the king's dream to him, Daniel praises God, who controls times and kings, gives wisdom to the wise and reveals deep and hidden things.
dan-2-44: Interpreting the king's dream, Daniel declares that the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed. It will crush all earthly empires and stand for ever.
dan-3-17-18: Facing the furnace, three young Jews tell the king that their God can save them. Even if he does not, they will never worship the king's gods. Their trust did not depend on rescue.
dan-3-24-25: King Nebuchadnezzar is astonished to see four men walking unharmed in the furnace instead of three bound men. The fourth, he says, looks like a son of the gods.
dan-4-34-35: After God humbled him with madness, Nebuchadnezzar regains his reason and praises the Most High, whose rule lasts for ever. No one can stop God's hand or question what he does.
dan-6-22: Daniel tells King Darius that God sent his angel to shut the lions' mouths, because he was found innocent before God and had done the king no wrong.
dan-6-26-27: King Darius orders his whole empire to revere Daniel's God. He is the living God whose kingdom will not be destroyed, who rescues and performs wonders, as he did for Daniel.
dan-7-13-14: In a vision, Daniel sees one like a son of man coming with the clouds to the Ancient of Days and receiving everlasting rule over all peoples. Jesus took the title Son of Man from this passage.
dan-7-18: An angel explains Daniel's vision of beasts: those empires will pass, but the holy people of the Most High will receive the kingdom and possess it for ever.
dan-7-27: The angel concludes that after the final oppressor is judged, all earthly rule will be given to the holy people of the Most High. God's kingdom will last for ever, and all rulers will obey him.
dan-9-9: In his prayer of confession for Israel, Daniel admits that the people have rebelled against God, yet mercy and forgiveness still belong to the Lord their God.
dan-9-18-19: Daniel pleads with God to hear and act for ruined Jerusalem. He asks not because Israel deserves it, but because of God's great mercy and for the sake of his own name.
dan-10-12: An angel tells Daniel not to be afraid. From the first day he humbled himself to seek understanding, his prayer was heard, and the angel came in response.
dan-10-18-19: Daniel recounts that a heavenly figure touched him and told him he was deeply loved, to have peace and be strong. As he spoke, Daniel felt his strength return.
dan-12-1: The angel tells Daniel that a time of unequalled distress will come, but Michael will protect his people. Everyone whose name is written in God's book will be rescued.
dan-12-2-3: The angel foretells a resurrection: many who sleep in the dust will wake, some to everlasting life and some to shame. The wise who lead others to righteousness will shine like stars.
dan-12-13: The angel tells Daniel personally to go on faithfully until his end. He will rest in death and then rise to receive his allotted inheritance at the end of the days.
hos-1-10: Right after naming Hosea's son "Not my people", God promised that Israel would one day be countless and called "children of the living God". Paul applies this to God's calling of Gentiles too.
hos-2-14-15: Picturing Israel as his unfaithful wife, God says he will lead her into the wilderness and speak tenderly to her. He will turn the Valley of Trouble into a door of hope.
hos-2-16-20: God promised that Israel would call him "my husband", not "my master", and forget the Baals. He would betroth her to himself for ever in righteousness, love, mercy and faithfulness.
hos-2-21-23: God promised that in that day heaven and earth would answer one another with rain and harvest. He would show love to those called "Not loved" and say to "Not my people", "You are my people."
hos-6-1-3: The people urge one another to return to the LORD, confident he will heal them quickly. God's reply in the next verses suggests this repentance was shallow, yet the call to know him still matters.
hos-11-1: God recalls loving Israel when the nation was a child and calling his son out of Egypt. Matthew sees this pattern repeated when Jesus returned from Egypt.
hos-11-3-4: God remembers teaching Israel to walk like a parent, holding them by the arms and healing them, though they did not realise it. He led them with kindness and love and bent down to feed them.
hos-11-8-9: Though Israel deserved destruction, God cries out that he cannot give them up. His compassion is stirred, and because he is God and not human, he will not destroy them in fierce anger.
hos-14-4-5: God promised repentant Israel that he would heal their unfaithfulness and love them freely, since his anger had turned away. He would be like dew to them, and they would blossom like a lily.
hos-14-7: God promised that restored Israel would again offer shelter to others, flourish like grain and vines, and become famous like the wine of Lebanon.
jol-2-12-13: After a devastating locust plague, God called Judah to return to him with all their heart, with fasting and weeping. Tear your hearts, not your clothes, for he is gracious and slow to anger.
jol-2-18-19: Joel reports that the LORD took pity on his people and promised to send grain, wine and oil to satisfy them, and to end their disgrace among the nations.
jol-2-21-22: Joel tells the scorched land and animals not to fear, because the LORD has done great things. Pastures would turn green again, and trees and vines would bear fruit.
jol-2-23-24: Joel calls the people of Zion to rejoice, because God would send autumn and spring rains as before. Their threshing floors would be full of grain and their vats overflow with wine and oil.
jol-2-25-27: God promised Judah that he would repay them for the years of harvest the locusts had destroyed. They would eat their fill, praise him, and know that he was among them.
jol-2-28-29: God promised that afterward he would pour out his Spirit on all kinds of people, young and old, men and women, even servants. Peter declared at Pentecost that this had begun.
jol-2-32: God promises, through Joel, that in the coming day of judgment everyone who calls on the LORD's name will be saved. Paul later quotes this to show salvation is open to anyone who calls on Jesus.
jol-3-16-17: Joel foresees the LORD roaring from Zion in judgment so that heaven and earth shake. Yet he will be a refuge and fortress for his people, dwelling among them in a holy Jerusalem.
jol-3-18: Joel pictures the coming age as overflowing abundance: mountains dripping with wine, hills flowing with milk, and a fountain from the LORD's house watering the dry valleys.
amo-5-4: In the middle of warnings of judgment, God tells Israel that if they seek him, they will live. Empty religion at their shrines would not save them.
amo-5-14-15: Amos urges Israel to seek good, not evil, so they may live and God truly be with them. If they hate evil, love good and practise justice, God may perhaps show mercy to a remnant.
amo-9-11-12: After announcing judgment, God promised to rebuild David's fallen house and restore its ruins. James at the Jerusalem council saw this fulfilled as Gentiles came to God.
amo-9-13-15: God promised a time of such abundance that harvests would overlap. He would restore his exiled people, they would rebuild and plant, and he would plant them in their land never to be uprooted.
oba-1-15-17: Obadiah warns Edom that the day of the LORD is near, and what they did to Judah will come back on them. But on Mount Zion there will be deliverance and holiness for God's people.
oba-1-21: Obadiah ends his prophecy against Edom by announcing that deliverers will go up to Mount Zion to rule, and the kingdom will belong to the LORD.
jon-2-1-2: From inside the great fish, Jonah prays and remembers that when he called to the LORD in distress, God answered him, hearing him even from the edge of death.
jon-2-6-7: Jonah describes sinking to the roots of the mountains, as if locked in for ever. When his life was ebbing away he remembered the LORD, and God brought him up from the pit.
jon-2-8-9: Jonah says those who cling to worthless idols give up God's love. He vows to sacrifice with thanksgiving and declares that salvation comes from the LORD alone.
jon-3-9-10: When Nineveh's king called everyone to repent, hoping God might relent, God saw that they turned from their evil ways and spared them from the destruction he had announced.
jon-4-2: Jonah angrily admits that he fled because he knew God is gracious, compassionate, slow to anger and rich in love, ready to spare even Israel's enemies. His complaint reveals God's mercy.
mic-4-1-3: Like Isaiah, Micah foresees the nations streaming to the LORD's mountain to learn his ways. God will settle their disputes, and they will beat their swords into ploughs and stop learning war.
mic-4-4: Micah pictures the peace of God's coming reign: everyone sitting under their own vine and fig tree with no one to frighten them. The LORD Almighty has promised it.
mic-4-5: Micah declares that while other nations follow their own gods, God's people will walk in the name of the LORD their God for ever.
mic-5-2: Micah foretold that from tiny Bethlehem would come a ruler for Israel whose origins are from ancient times. Matthew records that Jesus was born there in fulfilment of this.
mic-5-4-5: Micah describes the coming ruler standing to shepherd his people in the LORD's strength. His greatness will reach the ends of the earth, and he himself will be their peace.
mic-6-8: Answering a question about which sacrifices would please God, Micah says God has already shown what is good: to act justly, love faithfulness and mercy, and walk humbly with him.
mic-7-7-8: Surrounded by corruption, Micah resolves to watch for the LORD and wait for the God who saves him. He tells his enemy not to gloat: though he falls, he will rise, and God will be his light.
mic-7-9: Speaking for Israel, Micah accepts the LORD's anger because they have sinned. Yet he trusts that God will take up his case, bring him into the light and show his justice.
mic-7-18-19: Micah marvels that no god is like the LORD, who pardons sin and does not stay angry for ever, because he delights in mercy. He will trample our sins and throw them into the depths of the sea.
mic-7-20: Micah ends his book by trusting that God will show faithfulness to Jacob and unfailing love to Abraham, as he swore to their ancestors long ago.
nam-1-7: In a prophecy of judgment on Nineveh, Nahum pauses to declare that the LORD is good, a stronghold when trouble comes. He knows and cares for those who take refuge in him.
hab-2-3: God told Habakkuk that the vision of coming judgment and justice had an appointed time. Though it seemed slow, he should wait for it, because it would certainly come and not be late.
hab-2-4: God contrasts the proud, whose desires are not upright, with the righteous, who will live by faithfulness. Paul and Hebrews quote this to show that people are made right with God through faith.
hab-2-14: Amid judgments on proud empires, God declares that the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the LORD's glory as completely as water fills the sea.
hab-3-17-19: Habakkuk resolves that even if every crop fails and the flocks die, he will still rejoice in the God who saves him. The LORD gives him strength and sure footing like a deer on the heights.
zep-3-9-10: God promised to purify the speech of the peoples so all could call on him and serve him together. Even from distant Cush his scattered worshippers would bring offerings.
zep-3-11-12: God promised that he would remove the proud from Jerusalem, so his people would no longer be put to shame. A humble, lowly people would remain, trusting in the name of the LORD.
zep-3-13: God promised that the remnant of Israel would do no wrong and tell no lies. Like a safe flock, they would eat and lie down with no one to frighten them.
zep-3-14-15: Zephaniah calls Jerusalem to sing and rejoice with all her heart, because the LORD has ended her punishment and driven out her enemy. The King of Israel is with her, so she need not fear.
zep-3-16-17: Zephaniah tells Jerusalem not to fear, because the LORD is with her as a mighty saviour. He will delight in her, quiet her with his love and rejoice over her with singing.
zep-3-19-20: God promised to deal with Israel's oppressors, rescue the lame and gather the scattered. He would bring them home and turn their shame into honour and praise among all peoples.
hag-1-13: When the returned exiles finally obeyed and began rebuilding the temple, Haggai brought them a short message from God: "I am with you."
hag-2-4-5: God told Zerubbabel, Joshua the high priest and the people to be strong and keep working on the temple, because he was with them as he had promised at the exodus, and his Spirit remained among them.
hag-2-6-9: To builders discouraged by the modest new temple, God promised to shake the nations so their treasures would fill it. Its glory would be greater than Solomon's, and there he would give peace.
hag-2-19: God told the people that although the seed was not yet in the barn and the trees had not yet borne fruit, from the day they laid the temple's foundation he would bless them.
hag-2-23: God promised Zerubbabel, governor of Judah and heir of David, that he would make him like a signet ring, a sign of authority, because God had chosen him. It points to David's line continuing.
zec-1-3: God told the people, whose ancestors had refused to listen, to return to him, and he would return to them.
zec-1-16-17: God announced that he had returned to Jerusalem with mercy. His house would be rebuilt, the city measured for rebuilding, and its towns would again overflow with prosperity.
zec-2-4-5: An angel announced that Jerusalem would be so full of people and animals that it would have no walls. God himself would be a wall of fire around it and the glory within it.
zec-2-8-9: God declared that whoever harms his people touches the apple of his eye. He would raise his hand against the nations that plundered them.
zec-2-10-11: God calls Zion to sing for joy, because he is coming to live among them. Many nations will join themselves to the LORD and become his people.
zec-3-4-5: In Zechariah's vision, Joshua the high priest stands in filthy clothes, a picture of guilt. The angel orders them removed, declares his sin taken away and dresses him in clean garments.
zec-3-8-9: God tells Joshua and his fellow priests that they are a sign of what is coming: God will bring his servant, the Branch, and remove the guilt of the land in a single day.
zec-4-6: God told Zerubbabel that the temple would not be rebuilt by military might or human strength but by God's Spirit. The task would be completed by God's power.
zec-8-3-4: God promised to return to Zion and live in Jerusalem, which would be called the City of Truth. Elderly people would again sit in its streets, a sign of long life and peace.
zec-8-7-8: God promised to rescue his people from lands east and west and bring them to live in Jerusalem. They would be his people and he their God, in faithfulness and righteousness.
zec-8-12-13: God promised the remnant that crops would grow, vines would bear and the sky would give dew. Once a curse among the nations, they would now become a blessing, so they should not fear.
zec-8-16-17: God tells his restored people what he expects: speak truth to one another, judge fairly in the courts, do not plot harm against neighbours and do not love false oaths, because he hates these things.
zec-9-9-10: Zechariah foresees Jerusalem's righteous King coming humbly on a donkey, bringing salvation and peace to the nations. The Gospels show Jesus fulfilling this when he entered Jerusalem.
zec-9-11-12: Because of the blood of his covenant, God promised to free his captive people from the waterless pit. He calls these prisoners of hope back to their stronghold and promises double restoration.
zec-10-1: Zechariah tells the people to ask the LORD, not idols or fortune-tellers, for spring rain. God is the one who makes the storm clouds and gives showers for everyone's crops.
zec-10-6: God promised to strengthen Judah and save the northern tribes, bringing them back in compassion. It would be as if he had never rejected them, because he is their God and will answer them.
zec-12-1: Zechariah introduces a prophecy by naming its source: the LORD who stretched out the heavens, laid the earth's foundations and formed the human spirit within each person.
zec-12-10: God promised to pour a spirit of grace and prayer on Jerusalem. They would look on the one they pierced and mourn bitterly as for an only son. John applies this to Jesus' crucifixion.
zec-13-1: God foretold that in that day a fountain would be opened for David's house and Jerusalem's people to wash away their sin and impurity.
zec-13-9: God foretold that he would refine a remnant of his people through fire like silver and gold. They would call on him and he would answer, saying "They are my people", and they would say "The LORD is our God."
zec-14-8-9: Zechariah foresees living water flowing from Jerusalem toward both seas all year round. The LORD will be king over the whole earth, the only God, worshipped by one name.
mal-1-2: God opens Malachi's message by telling his discouraged people that he has loved them. When they question this, he points to how he chose Jacob and kept faith with his descendants.
mal-3-1: God announced that he would send a messenger to prepare his way, and then the Lord they sought would suddenly come to his temple. The Gospels identify the messenger as John the Baptist, preparing for Jesus.
mal-3-6: God reminds Israel that he does not change. That is the only reason Jacob's unfaithful descendants have not been destroyed: he stays true to his covenant even when they do not.
mal-3-7: God says Israel has turned away from his laws since their ancestors' days, yet he still invites them to return to him and he will return to them. They reply by asking how.
mal-3-10-11: God told Judah, who were withholding tithes, to bring the full tithe so the temple storehouse had food. He invited them to test him and see him send rain and harvest. It was a covenant call to Israel, not a formula for wealth.
mal-3-16-17: When those who revered the LORD talked together, God listened and had their names recorded in a book. He said they would be his treasured possession, spared like a son who serves his father.
mal-4-2: God promised that for those who honour his name, a sun of righteousness would rise with healing in its rays. They would leap for joy like calves released from the stall.
mat-1-21-23: An angel told Joseph that Mary's son was to be named Jesus, meaning "the LORD saves", because he would save his people from their sins. Matthew sees Isaiah's Immanuel sign fulfilled: God with us.
mat-4-4: When Satan tempted the fasting Jesus to turn stones into bread, Jesus quoted Deuteronomy: people do not live by bread alone but by every word from God. He relied on his Father, not his own power.
mat-5-3-10: Jesus promises that the humble, the grieving, the gentle and those who long for what is right belong to God's kingdom and will be comforted and satisfied. The kingdom reverses the world's idea of who is blessed.
mat-5-11-12: Jesus promises that those insulted, persecuted and slandered because they follow him are blessed and will have a great reward in heaven. They stand in line with the persecuted prophets.
mat-6-6: Jesus promises that the Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward private and sincere prayer. He is warning against praying to impress other people.
mat-6-8: Jesus tells his followers not to pile up empty words when they pray like the pagans, because their Father already knows what they need before they ask.
mat-6-9-13: Jesus gives his followers a model prayer. It puts God's name, kingdom and will first, then asks for daily bread, forgiveness as we forgive others, and protection from temptation and evil.
mat-6-14-15: Jesus explains that God's forgiveness and our forgiveness of others go together. Those who refuse to forgive others show that they have not truly received God's forgiveness.
mat-6-25-26: Jesus tells his followers not to worry about food, drink or clothing, since life is more than these. God feeds the birds, which do not farm, and they are worth far more to him.
mat-6-27-30: Jesus points out that worry cannot add a single hour to life. If God clothes wild flowers more splendidly than Solomon, he will surely clothe his people, so their faith should not be so small.
mat-6-31-34: Jesus promises that if his followers put God's kingdom and righteousness first, their Father, who knows their needs, will provide what they need. So they should not worry about tomorrow.
mat-7-7-8: Jesus promises that those who keep asking, seeking and knocking in prayer will receive, find and have the door opened. He encourages persistent prayer to a Father who answers.
mat-7-9-11: Jesus argues that if flawed human parents give their children good things rather than harmful ones, the heavenly Father will give good gifts even more surely to those who ask him.
mat-7-24-25: Ending the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus compares someone who hears and obeys his words to a wise builder on rock. When storms come, that house stands. Hearing without doing leads to collapse.
mat-8-2-3: A man with leprosy knelt and told Jesus he could heal him if he wanted to. Jesus touched him, saying, "I am willing", and the man was instantly healed. His touch showed compassion as well as power.
mat-8-16-17: Matthew records that Jesus drove out spirits and healed all the sick brought to him. He sees this as fulfilling Isaiah's words that the servant would take up our weaknesses and carry our diseases.
mat-9-2: When friends brought a paralysed man to Jesus, Jesus saw their faith and told the man to take heart because his sins were forgiven, showing that his deepest need was forgiveness.
mat-9-12-13: When criticised for eating with sinners, Jesus replied that the sick need a doctor, not the healthy. He came to call sinners, and told his critics to learn that God desires mercy more than sacrifice.
mat-9-21-22: A woman who had bled for years touched Jesus' cloak, believing it would heal her. Jesus turned, called her "daughter" and told her that her faith had made her well.
mat-9-36-38: Seeing the crowds harassed and helpless like sheep without a shepherd, Jesus felt compassion. He told his disciples the harvest was great but workers few, so they should pray for more.
mat-10-19-20: Sending out the twelve, Jesus told them that when they were arrested and put on trial, they need not worry what to say. The Spirit of their Father would give them the words.
mat-10-28-31: Jesus tells his followers not to fear those who can only kill the body, but to revere God. Not even a sparrow falls without the Father's knowledge, and they are worth far more than sparrows.
mat-10-32: Jesus promises that whoever openly acknowledges him before others, he will acknowledge before his Father in heaven. The next verse warns that the reverse is also true.
mat-10-39: Jesus states a paradox of discipleship: those who cling to their own life will lose it, but those who give up their life for his sake will find true life.
mat-10-42: Jesus promises that even a small kindness, like a cup of cold water given to one of his humblest followers because they belong to him, will not go unrewarded.
mat-11-28-30: Jesus promises rest to all who are worn out and weighed down, first those burdened by sin and the religious rules of his day. His yoke is his teaching, and following him, gentle and humble, brings real rest.
mat-12-18-21: Matthew quotes Isaiah's servant song to explain why Jesus avoided publicity. He is God's chosen servant who brings justice gently, without breaking the weak, and in whom the nations will hope.
mat-12-31: Jesus says every sin and slander can be forgiven, but not blasphemy against the Holy Spirit. He said this to Pharisees who called the Spirit's work in him the devil's work, a settled rejection of God.
mat-13-43: Jesus promises, explaining the parable of the weeds, that at the end of the age the righteous will shine like the sun in their Father's kingdom. He urges everyone to listen.
mat-14-27: When the terrified disciples saw Jesus walking on the lake at night and thought he was a ghost, he immediately reassured them: take courage, it is I, do not be afraid.
mat-16-18-19: After Peter confessed him as the Messiah, Jesus promised to build his church on this rock, and death itself would not overcome it. He gave Peter authority, the keys of the kingdom.
mat-16-24-25: Jesus tells his disciples that following him means denying themselves and taking up their cross. Those who try to save their own lives will lose them, but those who lose their lives for him will find life.
mat-17-5: At the transfiguration, a bright cloud covered the disciples and God's voice declared that Jesus is his beloved Son, with whom he is pleased. He commanded them to listen to him.
mat-18-3-4: When the disciples argued over who was greatest, Jesus said that unless they turn and become humble like little children, they will not enter the kingdom. The humblest is the greatest.
mat-18-10: Jesus warns his disciples not to look down on any of the little ones who belong to him, because their angels always have access to the Father in heaven.
mat-18-12-14: Jesus compares God to a shepherd who leaves ninety-nine sheep to search for one that has wandered off, and rejoices when he finds it. The Father does not want any of these little ones to be lost.
mat-18-19-20: Jesus promises that when two or three of his followers agree in his name, the Father will act on their request and he himself is among them. He said this while teaching on restoring a brother who sins.
mat-19-14: When the disciples tried to keep children away, Jesus told them to let the children come to him, because the kingdom of heaven belongs to people like them.
mat-19-26: After saying how hard it is for the rich to enter God's kingdom, Jesus tells his astonished disciples that salvation is impossible for humans, but with God everything is possible.
mat-19-28-29: Jesus promises that his disciples will reign with him when all things are renewed. Everyone who gives up home or family for his sake will receive far more and inherit eternal life.
mat-20-26-28: Jesus tells his disciples that greatness among them means serving others, just as he, the Son of Man, came not to be served but to serve and give his life as a ransom for many.
mat-21-21-22: Jesus promises, after the fig tree withered, that faith without doubt could even move a mountain and that believing prayer will be answered. This sits within his wider teaching on praying according to God's will.
mat-24-13: Jesus promises that whoever stands firm to the end will be saved. He says this while warning of persecution, false prophets and growing lawlessness before the end.
mat-24-30-31: Jesus foretells that he, the Son of Man, will appear on the clouds with power and great glory. He will send his angels with a loud trumpet to gather his chosen people from everywhere.
mat-24-35: Jesus declares that heaven and earth will pass away, but his words will never pass away. What he has said is more lasting than the universe itself.
mat-25-21: In Jesus' parable of the talents, the master praises the servant who used what he was given well, gives him greater responsibility and invites him to share his joy. It pictures faithful service rewarded.
mat-25-34: In his description of the final judgment, Jesus says the King will invite those blessed by his Father to inherit the kingdom prepared for them since the creation of the world.
mat-25-40: In the scene of final judgment, the King tells the righteous that whatever kindness they did for the least of his brothers and sisters, they did for him.
mat-26-26-28: At the Last Supper, Jesus gave his disciples bread as his body and the cup as his blood of the covenant, poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins. His death would seal the new covenant.
mat-28-5-7: At the empty tomb, an angel told the women not to be afraid. Jesus, who was crucified, had risen as he said. They were to see the place and quickly tell his disciples.
mat-28-18-20: Jesus promises to be with his disciples always, to the end of the age. The risen Jesus says this after claiming all authority and sending them to make disciples of every nation, baptising and teaching them.
mrk-1-14-15: Beginning his ministry in Galilee, Jesus announced that the appointed time had come and God's kingdom was near. He called people to repent and believe the good news.
mrk-2-5: Seeing the faith of the friends who lowered a paralysed man through the roof, Jesus first told him that his sins were forgiven, a claim only God could make.
mrk-2-17: When the religious leaders objected to him eating with tax collectors and sinners, Jesus said that doctors are for the sick. He came to call sinners, not those who think themselves righteous.
mrk-4-39-40: Woken in the boat during a violent storm, Jesus ordered the wind and waves to be still, and there was complete calm. Then he asked his disciples why they were so afraid and still had no faith.
mrk-5-34: Jesus told the woman who had been bleeding for twelve years and touched his cloak that her faith had made her well. She could go in peace, freed from her suffering.
mrk-5-36: When messengers told Jairus his daughter had died, Jesus overheard and told him not to be afraid but to keep believing. He then went on to raise the girl.
mrk-6-50: When his disciples, straining at the oars, saw him walking on the water and were terrified, Jesus spoke at once: take courage, it is I, do not be afraid. He then got into the boat and the wind stopped.
mrk-8-34-35: Jesus calls the crowd to understand that following him means denying themselves and taking up their cross. Whoever loses their life for him and the gospel will save it.
mrk-9-23: When a father asked Jesus to help his son "if you can", Jesus turned the doubt around: everything is possible for one who believes. The father then cried out, "Help my unbelief."
mrk-10-14-15: Jesus was indignant when his disciples turned children away. He told them to let the children come, because God's kingdom belongs to such as these, and only those who receive it like a child will enter.
mrk-10-27: When the disciples asked who could be saved if even the rich struggle, Jesus looked at them and said that for people it is impossible, but not for God, since God can do all things.
mrk-10-29-30: Jesus promises that anyone who leaves home or family for him and the gospel will receive a hundred times as much in this life, in the family of believers, along with persecutions, and eternal life to come.
mrk-10-45: Jesus explains the purpose of his life: the Son of Man did not come to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom that sets many free.
mrk-11-24: Jesus promises that whatever his disciples ask in prayer, trusting God, they will receive. The next verse ties this to forgiving others, and Scripture elsewhere links it to praying according to God's will.
mrk-13-11: Speaking of coming persecution, Jesus told his disciples not to worry beforehand about what to say when they were arrested and tried. The Holy Spirit would speak through them in that hour.
mrk-13-13: Jesus promises that the one who endures to the end will be saved, even though his followers will be hated by everyone because of his name.
mrk-13-26-27: After describing cosmic signs, Jesus tells his disciples that people will see the Son of Man coming in the clouds with great power and glory, and he will gather his chosen people from the ends of the earth.
mrk-13-31: Concluding his teaching on the end times, Jesus says the whole created order will pass away, yet his own words will remain for ever. His teaching is utterly reliable.
mrk-16-6-7: A young man in white told the startled women that the crucified Jesus had risen. They should tell his disciples, and Peter by name, that Jesus would meet them in Galilee, as he had said.
luk-1-30-33: The angel Gabriel told Mary not to be afraid, because God had favoured her. She would bear a son named Jesus, the Son of the Most High, who would reign on David's throne for ever.
luk-1-37: Gabriel told Mary that her relative Elizabeth, thought to be barren, was pregnant in her old age, because no word from God will fail. Mary's own unusual pregnancy was possible too.
luk-1-45: Filled with the Holy Spirit, Elizabeth told Mary that she was blessed because she had believed that the Lord would do what he had told her.
luk-1-46-50: In her song of praise, Mary rejoices in God her Saviour, who noticed his humble servant and did great things for her. His mercy reaches those who revere him in every generation.
luk-1-52-55: Mary praises God for turning the world's order upside down: bringing down rulers, lifting up the humble and feeding the hungry. He has helped Israel, remembering his mercy promised to Abraham.
luk-1-68-75: Filled with the Spirit after his son John's birth, Zechariah praises God for coming to redeem his people. He has raised up a saviour from David's line, keeping his oath to Abraham.
luk-1-76-79: Zechariah tells his newborn son John that he will be a prophet who prepares the Lord's way, teaching salvation through forgiveness. God's mercy will dawn like the sunrise on those in darkness.
luk-2-10-11: An angel told frightened shepherds near Bethlehem not to be afraid, because he brought good news of great joy for all people: the Saviour, the Messiah and Lord, had been born that day.
luk-2-14: A great company of angels praised God at Jesus' birth: glory to God in the highest heaven, and peace on earth among those he favours.
luk-2-29-32: Holding the baby Jesus in the temple, the elderly Simeon thanks God that he can now die in peace, because he has seen God's salvation, a light for the nations and glory for Israel.
luk-4-18-19: In his hometown synagogue, Jesus read Isaiah's words about one anointed by the Spirit to bring good news to the poor, freedom for prisoners and sight for the blind. He then said it was fulfilled in him.
luk-5-12-13: A man covered with leprosy fell before Jesus and begged to be made clean if Jesus was willing. Jesus reached out, touched him and said he was willing, and the leprosy left him at once.
luk-5-20: When friends lowered a paralysed man through a roof, Jesus saw their faith and told him his sins were forgiven, sparking debate about who but God can forgive sins.
luk-6-20-23: Jesus promises his disciples that those who are poor, hungry, grieving or hated because of him now are blessed. God's kingdom is theirs, they will be satisfied and laugh, and their reward in heaven is great.
luk-6-35-36: Jesus tells his followers to love their enemies, do good and lend without expecting repayment. Then they will be like the Most High, who is kind to the ungrateful and wicked; they should be merciful as he is.
luk-6-37-38: Jesus tells his followers not to judge or condemn but to forgive and give. God will give back to them generously, pressed down and overflowing, because the measure they use will be used for them.
luk-7-47-48: At a Pharisee's dinner, Jesus said the sinful woman who anointed his feet loved much because her many sins were forgiven. Then he told her directly: your sins are forgiven.
luk-8-48: Jesus spoke tenderly to the woman who, after twelve years of bleeding, had secretly touched his cloak. He called her daughter, said her faith had healed her, and sent her away in peace.
luk-8-50: On hearing that Jairus' daughter had died, Jesus told the grieving father not to fear but simply to believe, and she would be made well. He then raised her to life.
luk-9-23-24: Jesus told everyone that following him means denying themselves and taking up their cross daily. Those who try to hold on to their life will lose it, but those who lose it for him will save it.
luk-10-19-20: When the seventy-two returned excited that demons obeyed them, Jesus said he had given them authority over the enemy's power. But their real joy should be that their names are written in heaven.
luk-10-21: Full of joy in the Holy Spirit, Jesus thanks his Father for hiding the truth of the kingdom from the self-wise and revealing it to those who are like little children, because this pleased him.
luk-10-22: Jesus says the Father has entrusted everything to him. Only the Father truly knows the Son, and only the Son truly knows the Father, along with those to whom the Son chooses to reveal him.
luk-11-9-10: Jesus promises, after his parable of the friend at midnight, that those who keep asking, seeking and knocking will receive, find and have the door opened to them.
luk-11-11-13: Jesus promises that the heavenly Father will give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him. If sinful parents would never hand a child a snake instead of a fish, God will give far better gifts.
luk-12-6-7: Jesus reminds his followers that God does not forget even a cheap sparrow, and he has counted every hair on their heads. So they should not be afraid, because they are worth far more to him.
luk-12-8: Jesus promises that whoever openly acknowledges him before people, the Son of Man will acknowledge before the angels of God. He goes on to warn about denying him.
luk-12-22-24: Jesus tells his disciples not to worry about food or clothes, because life is more than these. Ravens neither sow nor store food, yet God feeds them, and his people are worth much more than birds.
luk-12-29-32: Jesus promises his disciples that if they seek God's kingdom, their needs for food and drink will be met too, since the Father knows what they need. The Father is pleased to give them the kingdom.
luk-12-33-34: Jesus urges his followers to sell possessions and give to the poor, storing up treasure in heaven that cannot be stolen or decay. Where their treasure is, their heart will be too.
luk-13-29-30: Jesus warns those who assumed they were in God's kingdom that people from every direction will come and feast in it. Some now considered last will be first, and some first will be last.
luk-15-4-7: Answering critics who grumbled about him welcoming sinners, Jesus told of a shepherd who searches for one lost sheep and joyfully carries it home. Heaven rejoices more over one sinner who repents.
luk-15-8-10: Jesus told of a woman who lights a lamp and sweeps her house until she finds a lost silver coin, then celebrates with her neighbours. In the same way, God's angels rejoice over one sinner who repents.
luk-15-20-24: In Jesus' parable of the lost son, the father runs to embrace his returning son before he can finish confessing. He clothes him and throws a feast, picturing God's joyful welcome to repentant sinners.
luk-18-7-8: After the parable of the persistent widow, Jesus assures his disciples that God will surely bring justice for his chosen ones who cry out to him, and will not delay. Yet he asks whether he will find faith when he returns.
luk-18-13-14: In Jesus' parable, a tax collector who simply begged God for mercy went home justified, unlike the proud Pharisee. Those who exalt themselves will be humbled, and the humble will be lifted up.
luk-18-16-17: When the disciples scolded people bringing babies to him, Jesus called the children to himself. God's kingdom belongs to such as these, and whoever does not receive it like a child will never enter it.
luk-18-27: When his hearers asked how anyone could be saved if even the rich struggled, Jesus answered that what is impossible for people is possible for God.
luk-18-29-30: Jesus promises, after Peter said they had left everything, that anyone who gives up home or family for God's kingdom will receive many times more in this age and eternal life in the age to come.
luk-19-9-10: After the tax collector Zacchaeus promised to repay those he had cheated, Jesus declared that salvation had come to his house. The Son of Man came to seek and save the lost.
luk-21-14-15: Jesus told his disciples that when they were persecuted and put on trial, they should not prepare their defence in advance. He would give them words and wisdom that no opponent could resist.
luk-21-18-19: Jesus promises that not a hair of his disciples' heads will perish, though he warned some would be betrayed and even killed. By standing firm they gain true life: ultimate safety, not escape from harm.
luk-21-27-28: Jesus foretells that people will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory. When these things begin, his followers should stand up and lift their heads, because their redemption is near.
luk-21-33: Jesus assures his disciples that even though heaven and earth will pass away, his words will certainly not pass away. They can stake everything on what he has said.
luk-22-19-20: At the Last Supper, Jesus gave the bread as his body given for them, to be shared in remembrance of him. The cup was the new covenant in his blood, poured out for them.
luk-23-34: While being crucified, Jesus prayed that his Father would forgive those who were killing him, because they did not know what they were doing. Meanwhile soldiers gambled for his clothes.
luk-23-42-43: When one of the criminals crucified beside him asked Jesus to remember him, Jesus promised that he would be with him in paradise that very day.
luk-24-5-7: Two men in shining clothes asked the frightened women why they looked for the living among the dead. Jesus had risen, as he told them in Galilee he would be crucified and rise on the third day.
luk-24-38-39: When the risen Jesus appeared and the disciples thought he was a ghost, he asked why they doubted and invited them to look at his hands and feet and touch him. He was truly alive in body.
luk-24-46-49: The risen Jesus explained that Scripture foretold the Messiah's suffering and resurrection and forgiveness preached to all nations. His disciples were witnesses, and he would send them power from on high.
jhn-1-12-13: John explains that everyone who receives Jesus and believes in his name is given the right to become a child of God. This new birth comes from God, not from ancestry or human effort.
jhn-1-14: John declares that the eternal Word became a human being and lived among us. His followers saw his glory, the glory of the Father's only Son, full of grace and truth.
jhn-1-16-17: John says that from the fullness of Christ we have all received one gift of grace after another. The law came through Moses, but grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.
jhn-1-29: Seeing Jesus approach, John the Baptist pointed him out as the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world, the sacrifice to which all the old offerings pointed.
jhn-3-3-5: Jesus told Nicodemus, a respected teacher, that no one can see or enter God's kingdom without being born again. This new birth comes from water and the Spirit, not from human effort.
jhn-3-14-15: Jesus promises eternal life to everyone who believes in him. As Moses lifted up a bronze snake so dying Israelites could look and live, he must be lifted up on the cross.
jhn-3-16-17: God promises eternal life to everyone who believes in his Son, whom he gave out of love for the world. God sent him not to condemn the world but to save it.
jhn-3-18: This verse explains that whoever believes in God's Son is not condemned, but whoever refuses to believe stands condemned already, because they have rejected the only Son of God.
jhn-3-36: The passage declares that whoever believes in the Son already has eternal life, but whoever rejects the Son will not see life; God's judgment remains on them.
jhn-4-13-14: Jesus promises that the water he gives becomes a spring within, welling up to eternal life. He told a Samaritan woman at a well that ordinary water only satisfies for a while.
jhn-4-23-24: Jesus told the Samaritan woman that the time had come when true worship would not depend on a holy mountain. God is spirit and seeks people who worship him in spirit and truth.
jhn-5-24: Jesus promises that whoever hears his word and believes the Father who sent him already has eternal life. They will not be condemned, because they have crossed over from death to life.
jhn-5-28-29: Jesus says a time is coming when all the dead will hear his voice and rise from their graves, those who did good to life and those who did evil to judgment. He claims the authority to raise the dead.
jhn-6-35: Jesus promises that whoever comes to him and believes in him will never go hungry or thirsty in their soul. After feeding the five thousand, he tells the crowd he is the bread of life.
jhn-6-37: Jesus promises that he will never turn away anyone who comes to him. Everyone the Father gives him will come.
jhn-6-39-40: Jesus promises that everyone who looks to the Son and believes will have eternal life, and he will raise them on the last day. His Father's will is that he lose none of those given to him.
jhn-6-47-48: Jesus promises that whoever believes in him has eternal life now. He again identifies himself as the bread of life, the true food the manna only pointed to.
jhn-6-51: Jesus promises that whoever eats the living bread from heaven will live for ever. The bread he will give for the life of the world is his own flesh, pointing to his death.
jhn-6-54-56: Jesus promises eternal life and resurrection to those who eat his flesh and drink his blood, strong imagery for receiving him and his death by faith. They live in him, and he in them.
jhn-6-63: When many disciples found his teaching hard, Jesus explained that the Spirit gives life, while human effort achieves nothing. His words are spirit and life, not a literal meal.
jhn-7-37-38: Jesus promises that rivers of living water will flow from those who believe in him; John explains this means the Spirit. He invited anyone thirsty to come to him on the last day of the Festival of Tabernacles.
jhn-8-12: Jesus promises that whoever follows him will not walk in darkness but will have the light that leads to life, because he is the light of the world.
jhn-8-31-32: Jesus promises people who had begun to believe that if they keep living by his teaching, they are truly his disciples. They will know the truth, and the truth will set them free.
jhn-8-34-36: Jesus says everyone who sins is a slave to sin. A slave has no permanent place in the family, but a son does, so if the Son sets people free, they are truly free.
jhn-8-51: Jesus promises that whoever keeps his word will never see death. He means eternal death, not physical dying, which his opponents misunderstood.
jhn-9-4-5: Before healing a man born blind, Jesus tells his disciples they must do God's work while it is day, because night is coming. While he is in the world, he is its light.
jhn-10-9-10: Jesus promises that whoever enters through him, the door for the sheep, will be saved and find pasture. Unlike the thief, he came so that people may have life in all its fullness.
jhn-10-11: Jesus declares that he is the good shepherd, who does not run away from danger but lays down his life for the sheep, pointing ahead to his death.
jhn-10-14-15: Jesus describes a close, mutual knowledge between himself and his sheep, like that between him and the Father. He gives his life for them.
jhn-10-27-29: Jesus promises that his sheep, who hear his voice and follow him, will never perish. No one can snatch them from his hand or from the Father's, who is greater than all.
jhn-10-30: Jesus claims that he and the Father are one. His opponents understood this as a claim to be God and picked up stones to kill him.
jhn-11-25-26: Jesus promises that whoever believes in him will live even after dying, and will never die eternally. At Lazarus' grave he told grieving Martha that he is the resurrection and the life, and asked if she believed it.
jhn-11-40: When Martha objected to opening Lazarus' tomb because of the smell, Jesus reminded her that he had said she would see God's glory if she believed. He then raised Lazarus.
jhn-12-24-25: Jesus explains that a grain of wheat must fall and die to produce a harvest. His own death will bring much fruit, and those who cling to life lose it while those who give it up keep it for eternity.
jhn-12-32: Jesus says that when he is lifted up from the earth, he will draw all people to himself. John notes this pointed to the kind of death he would die: crucifixion.
jhn-12-46: Jesus says he came into the world as light, so that no one who believes in him needs to remain in darkness.
jhn-13-34-35: At the Last Supper, Jesus gives his disciples a new command: love one another as he has loved them. This love will show everyone that they are his disciples.
jhn-14-1-3: Jesus promises his anxious disciples, the night before his death, that he is going to prepare a place for them in his Father's house. They are to trust him, because he will come back to take them to be with him.
jhn-14-6: When Thomas said they did not know the way, Jesus answered that he himself is the way, the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through him.
jhn-14-12-14: Jesus promises that believers will do the works he did and even greater ones, because he is going to the Father. He will do whatever they ask in his name, so that the Father is glorified in the Son.
jhn-14-15-17: Jesus promises his disciples that he will ask the Father to send another Helper, the Spirit of truth, who will live with them and in them for ever. Loving him means keeping his commands.
jhn-14-18: Jesus promises his disciples that he will not leave them alone like orphans after his death. He will come back to them, through his resurrection and his presence by the Spirit.
jhn-14-19-20: Jesus promises that although the world will soon stop seeing him, his disciples will see him, and because he lives they will live too. They will understand their union with him and the Father.
jhn-14-21: Jesus promises that the Father will love whoever keeps his commands, and Jesus will love them too and make himself known to them. Obedience is how real love for him shows.
jhn-14-23: Jesus promises, answering Judas (not Iscariot), that the Father and he will love anyone who loves him and keeps his word, and they will come and make their home with that person.
jhn-14-26: Jesus promised his disciples that the Father would send the Holy Spirit in his name to teach them everything and remind them of all he had said, a promise first for the apostles who passed on his words.
jhn-14-27: Jesus promises his disciples his own peace, unlike the passing peace the world gives. Because of this, their hearts need not be troubled or afraid.
jhn-15-1-2: Jesus calls himself the true vine and his Father the gardener. The Father removes fruitless branches and prunes the fruitful ones so they bear even more.
jhn-15-4-5: Jesus urges his disciples to stay joined to him, as a branch can only bear fruit while attached to the vine. Whoever remains in him bears much fruit, but apart from him they can do nothing.
jhn-15-7-8: Jesus promises that if his disciples remain in him and his words shape them, they can ask whatever they wish and it will be done. Their fruitfulness brings glory to the Father.
jhn-15-9-11: Jesus says he loves his disciples as the Father loves him, and calls them to stay in his love by keeping his commands. He tells them this so his joy may be in them and their joy complete.
jhn-15-12-13: Jesus commands his disciples to love each other as he has loved them. The greatest love is to lay down one's life for friends, as he was about to do.
jhn-15-15-16: Jesus calls his disciples friends, not servants, because he has shared with them everything from the Father. He chose them to bear lasting fruit, so the Father will give what they ask in his name.
jhn-15-26: Jesus promised his disciples that he would send the Helper, the Spirit of truth who comes from the Father. The Spirit would testify about Jesus, and so would they.
jhn-16-7: Jesus told his grieving disciples that his leaving was for their good, because unless he went away the Helper would not come. When he went, he would send the Spirit to them.
jhn-16-13-14: Jesus promised his disciples that the Spirit of truth would guide them into all truth and tell them what was to come. The Spirit would bring glory to Jesus by making him known.
jhn-16-20-22: Jesus promises his disciples that their grief will turn to joy, like a mother's after childbirth. They would weep while the world rejoiced, but when they saw him again no one could take that joy away.
jhn-16-23-24: Jesus promises that after his resurrection the Father will give whatever his disciples ask in Jesus' name. He urges them to ask and receive, so that their joy may be complete.
jhn-16-27: Jesus assures his disciples that the Father himself loves them, because they have loved Jesus and believed that he came from God. They can approach the Father directly.
jhn-16-33: Jesus tells his disciples plainly that they will have trouble in this world. But they can have peace in him and take courage, because he has overcome the world.
jhn-17-3: In his prayer before his arrest, Jesus defines eternal life as knowing the only true God and Jesus Christ whom he sent. It is a relationship, not merely endless time.
jhn-17-11: Jesus prays for his disciples, who will remain in the world after he leaves. He asks the Holy Father to protect them by his name, so that they may be one as the Father and Son are one.
jhn-17-15-17: Jesus does not ask the Father to take his disciples out of the world but to protect them from the evil one. He asks God to make them holy through the truth of his word.
jhn-17-20-23: Jesus prays for all who will believe through the apostles' message, asking that they be one as he and the Father are one. Their unity will show the world that God sent him and loves them.
jhn-17-24: Jesus asks the Father that those given to him may be with him where he is and see the glory the Father gave him, because the Father loved him before the world began.
jhn-17-26: Jesus ends his prayer saying he has made the Father known and will continue to do so, so that the Father's love for him may be in his followers, and he himself in them.
jhn-20-19-21: On the evening of his resurrection, Jesus came to his fearful disciples behind locked doors and said, "Peace be with you." He showed them his wounds and sent them as the Father had sent him.
jhn-20-22-23: The risen Jesus breathed on his disciples and told them to receive the Holy Spirit. He gave them authority to declare sins forgiven, or not, as they proclaimed his message.
jhn-20-27-29: Jesus invited doubting Thomas to touch his wounds, and Thomas confessed him as "my Lord and my God". Jesus then blessed all who would believe without having seen him.
jhn-20-31: John explains why he wrote his Gospel: so readers may believe that Jesus is the Messiah, the Son of God, and by believing have life in his name.
act-1-8: Before returning to heaven, Jesus promised the apostles that they would receive power when the Holy Spirit came on them. They would be his witnesses from Jerusalem to the ends of the earth.
act-2-17-18: At Pentecost Peter explained that the disciples were not drunk. Joel's prophecy was being fulfilled: in the last days God would pour out his Spirit on all kinds of people, sons and daughters, young and old.
act-2-21: Concluding his quotation of Joel, Peter told the crowd that everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved, and then showed that this Lord is Jesus.
act-2-38-39: When the crowd asked what to do, Peter told them to repent and be baptised in Jesus' name for forgiveness, and they would receive the Holy Spirit. This promise reaches their children and all whom God calls.
act-3-19-21: After healing a lame man, Peter urged the crowd to repent and turn to God so their sins would be wiped out. Times of refreshing would come, and God would send Jesus again at the final restoration.
act-4-12: On trial before the council, Peter declared that salvation is found in no one else but Jesus. No other name under heaven has been given by which people must be saved.
act-10-34-35: In the home of the Roman officer Cornelius, Peter realised that God does not show favouritism. He accepts people from every nation who revere him and do what is right.
act-10-43: Peter told Cornelius and his household that all the prophets testify about Jesus: everyone who believes in him receives forgiveness of sins through his name.
act-13-38-39: Preaching in a synagogue, Paul announced that forgiveness of sins is offered through Jesus. Everyone who believes is set right with God in every way the law of Moses could never achieve.
act-16-31: When the terrified jailer asked what he must do to be saved, Paul and Silas told him to believe in the Lord Jesus, and he and his household would be saved. His family heard and believed too.
act-18-9-10: In a night vision at Corinth, the Lord told Paul not to be afraid but to keep speaking. He promised that no one would harm him there, because many people in the city belonged to him.
act-26-17-18: Paul tells King Agrippa how Jesus sent him to the Gentiles to open their eyes, turning them from darkness to light and from Satan to God, so they could receive forgiveness and a place among God's people.
rom-1-16-17: Paul says he is not ashamed of the gospel, because it is God's power to save everyone who believes, Jew and Gentile alike. It reveals a righteousness from God received by faith from start to finish.
rom-3-21-24: Paul explains that God has now revealed a way to be right with him apart from the law, through faith in Jesus Christ. Everyone has sinned, and all who believe are justified freely by his grace.
rom-3-25-26: Paul explains that God presented Christ as a sacrifice of atonement, received through faith. This shows God is just: he does not ignore sin, yet he justifies those who trust in Jesus.
rom-4-5: Paul explains, using Abraham, that God counts as righteous the person who trusts him rather than relying on their own works, the God who justifies the ungodly.
rom-4-7-8: Paul quotes David's psalm to show that being right with God is a gift: blessed are those whose wrongs are forgiven and whose sins the Lord will never count against them.
rom-4-16-17: Paul explains that God's promise to Abraham comes by faith and grace, so it is guaranteed to all his spiritual children, not only those under the law. Abraham trusted the God who gives life to the dead.
rom-4-20-22: Paul says Abraham did not waver in unbelief at God's promise of a son, but grew strong in faith, fully convinced God could do what he had promised. That faith was credited to him as righteousness.
rom-5-1-2: Paul tells believers that, since they are made right with God through faith, they now have peace with him through Jesus. They stand in his grace and rejoice in the hope of sharing God's glory.
rom-5-3-5: Paul tells believers they can even rejoice in suffering, because it produces endurance, character and hope. This hope will not disappoint them, because God has poured his love into their hearts by the Spirit.
rom-5-6-8: Paul points out that people rarely die even for a good person. But God showed his love for us in this: Christ died for us while we were still powerless sinners.
rom-5-9-11: Paul reasons that if Christ's death reconciled us to God while we were enemies, then now that we are made right with him, we will surely be saved from judgment through his risen life.
rom-5-17: Paul contrasts Adam and Christ: through one man's sin death ruled. Far more, those who receive God's abundant grace and gift of righteousness will reign in life through Jesus Christ.
rom-5-20-21: Paul explains that the law made sin more visible, but where sin increased, God's grace increased even more. Grace now reigns, bringing eternal life through Jesus Christ.
rom-6-4-5: Paul tells believers that through baptism they were united with Christ in his death and burial. As Christ was raised, they too can now live a new life, and they will share his resurrection.
rom-6-14: Paul assures believers that sin will no longer be their master, because they are not under the law but under grace. This is a reason to resist sin, not permission to keep sinning.
rom-6-23: Paul contrasts two outcomes: sin pays its wage, which is death, but God gives a free gift, eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord. Life cannot be earned, only received.
rom-8-1-2: Paul declares that there is now no condemnation for those who belong to Christ Jesus. Through Christ, the Spirit who gives life has set them free from the power of sin and death.
rom-8-6: Paul contrasts two mindsets: a mind governed by sinful human nature leads to death, but a mind governed by the Spirit brings life and peace.
rom-8-9-11: Paul tells believers that God's Spirit lives in them, marking them as Christ's. The same Spirit who raised Jesus from the dead will also give life to their mortal bodies.
rom-8-14-16: Paul says that those led by God's Spirit are God's children. They have not received a spirit of fearful slavery but of adoption, so they cry "Abba, Father", and the Spirit confirms they belong to God.
rom-8-17: Paul explains that as God's children, believers are also his heirs, sharing Christ's inheritance. If they share in his sufferings, they will also share in his glory.
rom-8-18: Paul weighs present suffering against future glory and concludes that today's sufferings are not worth comparing with the glory God will reveal in his people.
rom-8-26-27: Paul assures believers that when they are weak and do not know what to pray, the Spirit himself prays for them with groans beyond words. God, who searches hearts, knows the Spirit's mind.
rom-8-28: Paul encourages suffering Christians. He does not call every event good. Rather, God works through all circumstances, hardship included, for the ultimate good of those who love him: growth in faith and final salvation.
rom-8-29-30: Paul explains God's purpose: those he foreknew he planned to shape into the likeness of his Son. He called them, made them right with him, and will surely bring them to glory.
rom-8-31-32: Paul asks who can stand against us if God is for us. Since God did not spare his own Son but gave him up for us all, he will surely give us everything we need with him.
rom-8-33-34: Paul asks who could accuse God's chosen people, since God himself declares them righteous. No one can condemn them, because Christ died, rose and now pleads for them at God's right hand.
rom-8-35-37: Paul lists hardships like persecution, hunger and the sword and asks whether any can separate us from Christ's love. Even when suffering, believers are more than conquerors through him who loved them.
rom-8-38-39: Paul declares his conviction that nothing in life or death, no spiritual power, nothing present or future, nor anything else in creation can separate believers from God's love in Christ Jesus.
rom-10-9-11: Paul explains that whoever openly confesses Jesus as Lord and truly believes God raised him from the dead will be saved. Quoting Isaiah, he adds that no one who trusts in him will be put to shame.
rom-10-12-13: Paul stresses that there is no difference between Jew and Gentile: the same Lord richly blesses all who call on him. Quoting Joel, he says everyone who calls on the Lord's name will be saved.
rom-11-29: Speaking of Israel's future, Paul says that God never takes back his gifts or his call. His commitments to his people are irrevocable.
